Write your audit to `audit.md` in this directory using the Write tool. Cite every finding as `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers taken from the `head/` files. Follow your auditor skill's output format and end the file with its machine-readable verdict trailer.

## Sprint 1: Review the pull request in pr/

The change under review is `pr/head.diff` (unified diff, base to head). The files before the change are under `pr/base/`, after it under `pr/head/`; `pr/PR.md` is the pull request description and is the implementation report for this sprint.

## Success Criteria

review the pull request, report each defect it introduces with the file and line it sits on, and give a merge verdict

review the pull request, report each defect it introduces with the file and line it sits on, and give a merge verdict

## Task

# Task: review a pull request

The directory `pr/` holds one pull request against a repository of shell scripts, tests and documentation, frozen for evaluation. The change: sprint-259 tasks and seeders (implementers D, E) — sixteen frozen-suite tasks under grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/tasks/ (bugfix-01…04, refactor-01…04 by D: synthetic planted defe….

- `pr/head/` — every touched file after the change

Review the change as the senior technical reviewer for the repository: find the defects it introduces and decide whether it can merge. Do not change any file under `pr/`.

head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:498 — bare `! grep -rqF` inside the for loop is inert under bats (ERR trap and set -e skip `!`-inverted commands); the "no hidden byte reached the sandbox/snapshots/transcripts" assertion cannot fail (also line 503); reproduced on bats 1.13.0
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:864 — envelope_texts never reads anchor_line; real dissent envelopes carry anchor "path:symbol" + anchor_line with no file/line, so every defect caught only by the adversarial review or audit is graded as missed and absent from flags
head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:16 — BATS_BIN is the author's personal dotfiles path; the symlink at line 48 dangles elsewhere and the stub PATH (line 51) only finds bats in /usr/bin, so AG-2 and AG-7 fail on any other host (bats is /usr/local/bin here)
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:710 — tarfile.data_filter / extractall(filter=) need Python ≥3.11.4; unchecked host interpreter (3.11.2 here) makes every run with a snapshot bundle exit 2 "internal error"
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1091 — an unparseable base regression run sets base_ok=[] so newly_failing is always empty for exit-status-only regression commands; an unparseable final run reports every base test newly failing even at rc 0
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:652 — all_pass ignores rc and timed_out; a suite that prints its summary then hangs or crashes is green for gate accuracy and self-checks, and a forged summary line is never cross-checked against rc
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:964 — "hidden" substring and ABS_WORD on quoted route strings flag rg --hidden, grep "/api/users", ls /home as contamination; first hit short-circuits so one benign hit drops the run
head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:501 — bare negations at 501, 502, 505, 512, 513 are inert; the DEC-0413 ids-only and no-source/eval checks cannot fail
head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:189 — bare `! grep -qF` is inert; SC-7 would not notice src/real.sh being excluded
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:452 — hard dependency on evals/harness/freeze.sh, and the PR title's sixteen tasks and freeze are not in the diff; VS-1 (validate-suite.bats:32-44) counts committed tasks absent from this change
head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:227 — patch invoked without --batch/-f and with inherited stdin; a missing-file prompt blocks the seeder on a TTY
head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:196 — counts() reads the last line of stdout+stderr combined; a trailing stderr warning yields 0/0 and a spurious proof failure
head/evals/harness/seed-bugfix-tasks.sh:43 — header says refusals do not count toward --select, but a post-selection no-secrets refusal consumes a slot without back-fill
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:517 — on TimeoutExpired only the docker client is killed; the container keeps a rw mount into grading/<label> and the next fresh_dir can race it
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:213 — yq is required but never checked; a missing binary surfaces as "internal error: FileNotFoundError" instead of a startup usage error
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1045 — grade() is 98 lines (load_task 100); split per concern
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:53 — 113-column header line, two sentences merged
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (= pr/PR.md)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff`: the cycle-130 ablation grader (`evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh`), the bug-fix and refactor task seeders (`seed-bugfix-tasks.sh`, `seed-refactor-tasks.sh`, `lib/seed_tasks.py`), the bd-8o5rx generated-path exclusion in `seed-corpus-from-record.sh`, the `source.churn` schema in `validate-suite.sh`, the regenerated pr-14/pr-15 key manifests, and six bats suites.

Much of it is careful work: every history path is checked before it touches disk (`safe_path`, `safe_rel`, `tarfile.data_filter`), mount-owned paths are refused by name, the grader never sources or evals anything, grade.json is written atomically, the generated-path rule is correct and tested at both the seeding and `--build-manifest` ends (SC-7, SC-8), the churn schema rejects booleans, and the pr-14/pr-15 checksums in `SHA256SUMS` match the regenerated manifests (verified with `sha256sum -c`).

Three defects block the merge. The hidden-test leak assertions added to `pipeline-run.bats` cannot fail (bare `!` is inert in bats; reproduced on bats 1.13.0). The grader's envelope parser never reads `anchor_line`, so every defect caught only by the adversarial dissent is graded as missed — reproduced against this very review's dissent envelope. And `ablation-grade.bats` hard-codes the author's personal bats path, so the bats-runner tests fail on any host where bats is not in `/usr/bin` (it is `/usr/local/bin/bats` here).

Local test run: the three new suites cannot be executed from the frozen `pr/head/` snapshot (the snapshot drops the executable bit and the suites reach for `evals/graders/no-secrets.sh`, `evals/harness/freeze.sh` and `grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke/`, none of which is in the PR). The diff itself records mode 100755 for the scripts, so that is a snapshot artefact, not a defect. Reviewed by reading every head file and by targeted reproduction of the mechanics in question.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Testing — the hidden-leak assertions are inert

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:498` — the `! grep -rqF "$f" …` inside the `for` loop never fails the test: bash skips the ERR trap and `set -e` for a `!`-inverted command, so a hidden-test byte (`sealed-case-7f3a`, `sealed-shape-91c2`, `sealed-patch-c0de`) present in the sandbox, snapshots or transcripts passes silently. Same at `head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:503` (`! git … grep -q -e 'sealed-'`). Only line 504 is effective, and only because it is the last command of the test.
**File:** `head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:498-503`
**Issue:** The new "frozen-suite layout" test is the only check of AC-2.6 / AC-5.5 ("no byte of any hidden/ file reached the sandbox, its git history or the snapshots"), and two of its three assertions are no-ops. Reproduced on bats 1.13.0 with a three-case file: a bare `! grep -q x <<<"x"` mid-test passes; the same line as the last command, or with `|| false`, fails.
**Why This Matters:** A leak of the hidden tests into the agent's sandbox is the one failure that invalidates the whole ablation. A guard that cannot fire is worse than none: it reports the property as verified.
**Required Fix:** Use `run ! grep -rqF "$f" …` (bats ≥1.5) or append `|| false`, as `seed-bugfix.bats:93` and `:109` already do. Apply the same fix to the other new inert negations listed under Observations §4.
**Reference:** bats-core writing-tests: "`! command` does not fail the test; use `run !`". bash(1) `set -e`: "…or if the command's return value is being inverted with !".

### 2. Grading — dissent findings never count toward recall

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:864-867` — `envelope_texts` emits the raw `anchor` string and a `file`/`path` + `line`/`line_start`/`start_line` pair, but the dissent envelopes carry neither: a real finding is `{"anchor": "evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:envelope_texts", "anchor_line": 864, "anchor_line_end": …}` with `file`, `path` and `line` all absent (this review's own `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-review.json`, every finding). The symbol anchor has no digits, so `citations()` yields nothing; `anchor_line` is never read. Every defect that only the review or audit dissent caught is graded as missed and is absent from `flags`.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:862-867`
**Issue:** The header promises "each finding's anchor (and file:line) in eval/adversarial-{review,audit}.json" (`ablation-grade.sh:96`), and AG-8 passes only because its hand-written envelopes use `anchor: "lib/x.sh:20"` and `file`+`line`, shapes `adversarial-review.sh` does not produce (its FR-4 contract is `anchor_line`/`anchor_line_end`, `adversarial-review.sh:28`, `:608-617`).
**Why This Matters:** The arm comparison the grader exists for (DEC-0420) is skewed against every arm whose gates run the dissent: their recall is under-counted exactly where the dissent adds value.
**Required Fix:** When `anchor_line` is an int, emit `f"{anchor.split(':', 1)[0]}:{anchor_line}"` (a `-{anchor_line_end}` range when present), keeping the existing `anchor` / `file`+`line` paths; add an AG-8 case whose envelope uses the real FR-4 shape.
**Reference:** `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:28` ("each finding may carry anchor_line / anchor_line_end (the head-file line, or range…)").

### 3. Fast-gate parity — the grader suite only runs on the author's machine

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:16` — `BATS_BIN="$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats"` is a personal dotfiles path; `ln -s "$BATS_BIN" "$T/bin/bats"` (`:48`) is a dangling symlink everywhere else, and the stub container PATH is `$T/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` (`:51`). On any host whose bats is not in `/usr/bin` (this one: `/usr/local/bin/bats`) the in-"image" `bats --tap tests` is exit 127, `run_suite` falls back to `parse_error: true, passed 0`, and AG-2 (`"2/3"`, `:268`) and AG-7 (`"3/3 false"`, `:352`) fail.
**File:** `head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:16`, `:48`, `:51`
**Issue:** The header even states the design ("`bats` is the operator's bats-core", `:11`). A CI runner or a second reviewer cannot run the grader's test suite green.
**Why This Matters:** `FAST-GATE:` the sprint's self-check cannot be reproduced; a failing-by-construction suite carries the weight of a test failure.
**Required Fix:** `BATS_BIN="${LOA_SEED_BATS:-$(command -v bats)}"` and `skip` when empty; or symlink `$(command -v bats)` and resolve its `libexec` the way bats-core's own wrapper does.

---

## Observations

### 1. Portability of the grader's host interpreter

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:710` — `tarfile.data_filter` and `extractall(…, filter=keep)` (`:714`) exist only on Python ≥3.12 or the 3.11.4 / 3.10.12 / 3.9.17 backports. The grader runs on the host interpreter, which is never checked: on Python 3.11.2 (this host; `'data_filter' in dir(tarfile)` → False) every run that has an IMPLEMENT or FIX1 bundle dies in `extract_snapshot` with `AttributeError`, caught at `:1290` as "internal error" exit 2, and no grade is written.
**Suggestion:** Guard with `getattr(tarfile, "data_filter", None)` and fall back to the explicit member checks `keep` already does (absolute, `..`, link targets), or state the interpreter floor in the header and `die` early.
**Benefit:** A grade refused for an interpreter version looks exactly like a tool failure in a batch.

### 2. Regression and pass/fail semantics

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1091` — when the base regression run is unparseable, `base_ok = []`, so `newly_failing` is always empty: a `regression_command` that reports through its exit status only (neither pytest nor TAP) can never surface a regression, although `run_suite`'s fallback synthesises ids and a `bad` set for exactly that case. The converse branch (`:1092-1093`) reports every base test as newly failing when only the final run is unparseable, even at rc 0, so `final.passed == final.total` can coexist with a full `newly_failing` list, contradicting the fallback rule at `:86-88`. (Dissent DISS-003, DISS-C-003 — confirmed.)
**Suggestion:** Derive `newly` from the fallback ids when both runs are fallback (`rf["rc"] != 0` → all of `base_ok`, else none) and expose `regressions.parse_error` so consumers can exclude the row.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:652-653` — `all_pass` ignores `rc` and `timed_out`. A suite that prints its complete summary and then hangs (rc 124) or crashes in teardown is green for `verdict_accuracy_per_gate`, `suite_green_*` and the self-checks; conversely nothing cross-checks rc against the parsed line, so agent-authored code imported by the hidden tests (a new root `conftest.py` the fixture lacks is not restored by `prepare`, `:657-674`) can print a forged `N passed in 0.1s` and `os._exit(0)`. (Dissent DISS-002, DISS-C-002 — confirmed as a gap; exploit requires a gaming agent.)
**Suggestion:** Treat `rc != 0` with a clean summary, or `rc == 0` with failures, as `parse_error: true`; require `not timed_out` in `all_pass`; consider removing `conftest.py` / `pytest.ini` / `pyproject.toml` / `setup.cfg` / `tox.ini` not present in the fixture before running.

### 3. Contamination false positives

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:964` — `"hidden" in low` fires on `rg --hidden`, `fd --hidden`, a Grep pattern such as `display: hidden`, or any CSS/HTML edit; `ABS_WORD` (`:977-980`) treats a quoted route string like `grep -rn "/api/users" src/` as a filesystem path, and `/home`, `/root`, `/mnt`, `/srv` are outside the container allow-list (`:949`), so `ls /home` is `outside_path`. The first hit short-circuits (`:1034`), so one benign hit marks the run contaminated and downstream aggregation drops it. The header calls the scan a lower bound on leakage; it is also an unbounded source of false flags. (Dissent DISS-C-001 — confirmed.)
**Suggestion:** Match `hidden` as a path component (`(^|/)hidden(/|$)`) on path fields and path-shaped Bash words; record every hit in a `contamination_hits` list and keep `contaminated` as the first.

### 4. More inert negated assertions

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:501` — `! grep -n 'graded_at\|test_\|slug\|…'` and `:502`, `:505`, `:512`, `:513` are mid-test bare negations: the DEC-0413 "ids only in every summary field" and "no `source`/`eval` in the grader" checks cannot fail (`:463` and `:514` work only as the last command of their tests). Same at `head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:189` (`! grep -qF 'excluded generated path: src/real.sh'`), so SC-7 would not notice a real file being excluded.
**Suggestion:** `run !` or `|| false`, as in finding 1.

### 5. Report and scope

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:452` — the grader hard-depends on `evals/harness/freeze.sh` (also `ablation-grade.bats:521`, `:569`) and the PR title promises "sixteen frozen-suite tasks under grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/tasks/" and "the freeze", but the diff contains neither a `freeze.sh`, a `MANIFEST.sha256`, nor any task directory; `validate-suite.bats:32-44` (VS-1) now counts the committed `tasks/` that are not in this change. `reviewer.md` is the PR description and has no `## AC Verification` walkthrough, so none of the sprint-259 ACs it cites (AC-2.3, 2.5, 2.6, 2.9, 10.1) can be checked file:line here.
**Suggestion:** Either include the tasks and freeze in the change or state in the report which earlier commit shipped them; add the AC walkthrough.

### 6. Seeder robustness

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:227` — `patch -s -p1 --no-backup-if-mismatch -i` without `--batch`/`-f` and with stdin inherited: a hunk whose file is missing from the fixture makes `patch` prompt "File to patch:" and the seeder blocks on a TTY. The grader passes `--batch --forward` (`ablation-grade.sh:1175`); mirror it.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:196-198` — `counts()` reads the last line of stdout+stderr concatenated; a stderr warning printed after pytest's summary makes passed = failed = 0 and the proof fails as "not red at base" / "not green at reference" for a sound commit. Parse stdout, or search the last few lines for the summary pattern as the grader does (`ablation-grade.sh:549-553`).
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/seed-bugfix-tasks.sh:43-44` — the header says refusals and skips "do not count" toward `--select`, but a no-secrets refusal after selection (`seed_tasks.py:588-592`) consumes a slot and is not back-filled from the remaining candidates.

### 7. Grader robustness

- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:517-521` — on `TimeoutExpired` only the `docker run` client is killed; the container keeps its rw bind mount into `grading/<label>` and the next `fresh_dir(grading)` (`:1053`) can race its writes. Name the container and `docker kill` it on timeout. (Dissent DISS-C-004 — plausible, unreproduced.)
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:213` — `yq` is required (`load_yaml`) but never checked; a missing binary is reported as "internal error: FileNotFoundError" rather than a usage error at startup, unlike docker (`docker_ready`, `:471`).

### 8. Complexity and style

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1045-1142` — `grade()` is 98 lines with the build / review-catch branches, regressions, refactor structural and snapshot accuracy inlined; `load_task()` (`:319-419`) is 100 lines. SIMPLICITY[shrink]: split per concern (`grade_build`, `grade_snapshots`, `grade_review_catch`) so each check is testable alone. `head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:53` is a 113-column header line (two sentences merged). Over-engineering pass otherwise clean — net: -0 lines possible (split, don't delete).

---

## Cross-Model Observations

Dissent envelope: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-review.json`, status `reviewed`, primary gpt-5.5-pro, companion claude-headless (`independent_voice`), 7 findings.

| Finding | Triage |
|---------|--------|
| DISS-001 (BLOCKING) envelope_texts ignores anchor_line | Confirmed against the real envelope shape → Changes Required §2 |
| DISS-002 (BLOCKING) all_pass ignores rc / timed_out | Confirmed gap, hang-after-summary is uncommon → Observations §2 (MEDIUM) |
| DISS-003 (BLOCKING) unparseable regression base → newly_failing always [] | Confirmed → Observations §2 (MEDIUM) |
| DISS-C-001 contamination false positives | Confirmed → Observations §3 (MEDIUM) |
| DISS-C-002 forged summary / no rc cross-check | Confirmed gap, needs a gaming agent → folded into Observations §2 |
| DISS-C-003 final-run parse_error → all base tests newly failing | Confirmed → folded into Observations §2 |
| DISS-C-004 orphaned container on client timeout | Plausible, unreproduced → Observations §7 (LOW) |

## Rejected dissent payloads

None. `metadata.rejected_summary` is empty and the named sidecar `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-rejected-review.jsonl` has 0 rows.

---

## Acceptance Criteria Check

### Task 1.1: the change in `pr/head.diff`

| Criterion | Status | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| "review the pull request, report each defect it introduces with the file and line it sits on, and give a merge verdict" (sprint.md) | Done | 3 blocking defects, 11 observations, each cited `head/<path>:<line>`; verdict below |
| Sprint-259 ACs named by the PR (AC-2.3, 2.5, 2.6, 2.9, 10.1) | Not verifiable | No `## AC Verification` in reviewer.md; the tasks/freeze the title names are not in the diff (Observations §5) |

---

## Security Checklist

- [x] No hardcoded secrets or credentials (SHA256SUMS verified; no-secrets scan is invoked by both seeders)
- [x] Input validation at trust boundaries: `safe_path`/`safe_rel`, mount-owned refusal, `data_filter`, symlink handling in `copy_tree`/`prepare`
- [x] No `source`/`eval` of variable content in the grader; argument-vector subprocess calls throughout
- [ ] Hidden-test leak guard effective — NO (Changes Required §1)
- [ ] Gaming resistance of pass/fail parsing — gap (Observations §2)
- [x] Error messages carry ids only in grade.json (by inspection; the test for it is inert, Observations §4)

---

## Code Quality Summary

**Strengths:**
- Path safety and trust-boundary discipline in both the seeders and the grader.
- Atomic `grade.json` write; byte-identical regrade by design (no timestamps or scratch paths).
- Generated-path exclusion (bd-8o5rx) correct at both ends with matching tests; `source.churn` schema strict.

**Areas for Improvement:**
- Negative assertions in bats must use `run !` or `|| false`.
- Test infrastructure must not depend on one operator's machine.
- Parse-fallback semantics should be the same for hidden tests, regressions and gate accuracy.

---

## Next Steps

1. Fix the three blocking items (inert leak assertions, `anchor_line` in `envelope_texts`, portable `BATS_BIN`).
2. Address the inert negations in Observations §4 in the same pass.
3. Add an `## AC Verification` section to the report, and either include the tasks/freeze or name the commit that shipped them.
4. Request another review via `/review-sprint sprint-1`.

The change under review is `pr/head.diff`: the cycle-130 ablation grader (`evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh`), the bug-fix and refactor task seeders (`seed-bugfix-tasks.sh`, `seed-refactor-tasks.sh`, `lib/seed_tasks.py`), the bd-8o5rx generated-path exclusion in `seed-corpus-from-record.sh`, the `source.churn` schema in `validate-suite.sh`, the regenerated pr-14/pr-15 key manifests, and six bats suites.

Much of it is careful work: every history path is checked before it touches disk (`safe_path`, `safe_rel`, `tarfile.data_filter`), mount-owned paths are refused by name, the grader never sources or evals anything, grade.json is written atomically, the generated-path rule is correct and tested at both the seeding and `--build-manifest` ends (SC-7, SC-8), the churn schema rejects booleans, and the pr-14/pr-15 checksums in `SHA256SUMS` match the regenerated manifests (verified with `sha256sum -c`).

Three defects block the merge. The hidden-test leak assertions added to `pipeline-run.bats` cannot fail (bare `!` is inert in bats; reproduced on bats 1.13.0). The grader's envelope parser never reads `anchor_line`, so every defect caught only by the adversarial dissent is graded as missed — reproduced against this very review's dissent envelope. And `ablation-grade.bats` hard-codes the author's personal bats path, so the bats-runner tests fail on any host where bats is not in `/usr/bin` (it is `/usr/local/bin/bats` here).

Local test run: the three new suites cannot be executed from the frozen `pr/head/` snapshot (the snapshot drops the executable bit and the suites reach for `evals/graders/no-secrets.sh`, `evals/harness/freeze.sh` and `grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke/`, none of which is in the PR). The diff itself records mode 100755 for the scripts, so that is a snapshot artefact, not a defect. Reviewed by reading every head file and by targeted reproduction of the mechanics in question.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

## Changes Required

### 1. Testing — the hidden-leak assertions are inert

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:498` — the `! grep -rqF "$f" …` inside the `for` loop never fails the test: bash skips the ERR trap and `set -e` for a `!`-inverted command, so a hidden-test byte (`sealed-case-7f3a`, `sealed-shape-91c2`, `sealed-patch-c0de`) present in the sandbox, snapshots or transcripts passes silently. Same at `head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:503` (`! git … grep -q -e 'sealed-'`). Only line 504 is effective, and only because it is the last command of the test.
**File:** `head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:498-503`
**Issue:** The new "frozen-suite layout" test is the only check of AC-2.6 / AC-5.5 ("no byte of any hidden/ file reached the sandbox, its git history or the snapshots"), and two of its three assertions are no-ops. Reproduced on bats 1.13.0 with a three-case file: a bare `! grep -q x <<<"x"` mid-test passes; the same line as the last command, or with `|| false`, fails.
**Why This Matters:** A leak of the hidden tests into the agent's sandbox is the one failure that invalidates the whole ablation. A guard that cannot fire is worse than none: it reports the property as verified.
**Required Fix:** Use `run ! grep -rqF "$f" …` (bats ≥1.5) or append `|| false`, as `seed-bugfix.bats:93` and `:109` already do. Apply the same fix to the other new inert negations listed under Observations §4.
**Reference:** bats-core writing-tests: "`! command` does not fail the test; use `run !`". bash(1) `set -e`: "…or if the command's return value is being inverted with !".

### 2. Grading — dissent findings never count toward recall

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:864-867` — `envelope_texts` emits the raw `anchor` string and a `file`/`path` + `line`/`line_start`/`start_line` pair, but the dissent envelopes carry neither: a real finding is `{"anchor": "evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:envelope_texts", "anchor_line": 864, "anchor_line_end": …}` with `file`, `path` and `line` all absent (this review's own `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-review.json`, every finding). The symbol anchor has no digits, so `citations()` yields nothing; `anchor_line` is never read. Every defect that only the review or audit dissent caught is graded as missed and is absent from `flags`.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:862-867`
**Issue:** The header promises "each finding's anchor (and file:line) in eval/adversarial-{review,audit}.json" (`ablation-grade.sh:96`), and AG-8 passes only because its hand-written envelopes use `anchor: "lib/x.sh:20"` and `file`+`line`, shapes `adversarial-review.sh` does not produce (its FR-4 contract is `anchor_line`/`anchor_line_end`, `adversarial-review.sh:28`, `:608-617`).
**Why This Matters:** The arm comparison the grader exists for (DEC-0420) is skewed against every arm whose gates run the dissent: their recall is under-counted exactly where the dissent adds value.
**Required Fix:** When `anchor_line` is an int, emit `f"{anchor.split(':', 1)[0]}:{anchor_line}"` (a `-{anchor_line_end}` range when present), keeping the existing `anchor` / `file`+`line` paths; add an AG-8 case whose envelope uses the real FR-4 shape.
**Reference:** `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:28` ("each finding may carry anchor_line / anchor_line_end (the head-file line, or range…)").

### 3. Fast-gate parity — the grader suite only runs on the author's machine

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:16` — `BATS_BIN="$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats"` is a personal dotfiles path; `ln -s "$BATS_BIN" "$T/bin/bats"` (`:48`) is a dangling symlink everywhere else, and the stub container PATH is `$T/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` (`:51`). On any host whose bats is not in `/usr/bin` (this one: `/usr/local/bin/bats`) the in-"image" `bats --tap tests` is exit 127, `run_suite` falls back to `parse_error: true, passed 0`, and AG-2 (`"2/3"`, `:268`) and AG-7 (`"3/3 false"`, `:352`) fail.
**File:** `head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:16`, `:48`, `:51`
**Issue:** The header even states the design ("`bats` is the operator's bats-core", `:11`). A CI runner or a second reviewer cannot run the grader's test suite green.
**Why This Matters:** `FAST-GATE:` the sprint's self-check cannot be reproduced; a failing-by-construction suite carries the weight of a test failure.
**Required Fix:** `BATS_BIN="${LOA_SEED_BATS:-$(command -v bats)}"` and `skip` when empty; or symlink `$(command -v bats)` and resolve its `libexec` the way bats-core's own wrapper does.

## Observations

### 1. Portability of the grader's host interpreter

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:710` — `tarfile.data_filter` and `extractall(…, filter=keep)` (`:714`) exist only on Python ≥3.12 or the 3.11.4 / 3.10.12 / 3.9.17 backports. The grader runs on the host interpreter, which is never checked: on Python 3.11.2 (this host; `'data_filter' in dir(tarfile)` → False) every run that has an IMPLEMENT or FIX1 bundle dies in `extract_snapshot` with `AttributeError`, caught at `:1290` as "internal error" exit 2, and no grade is written.
**Suggestion:** Guard with `getattr(tarfile, "data_filter", None)` and fall back to the explicit member checks `keep` already does (absolute, `..`, link targets), or state the interpreter floor in the header and `die` early.
**Benefit:** A grade refused for an interpreter version looks exactly like a tool failure in a batch.

### 2. Regression and pass/fail semantics

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1091` — when the base regression run is unparseable, `base_ok = []`, so `newly_failing` is always empty: a `regression_command` that reports through its exit status only (neither pytest nor TAP) can never surface a regression, although `run_suite`'s fallback synthesises ids and a `bad` set for exactly that case. The converse branch (`:1092-1093`) reports every base test as newly failing when only the final run is unparseable, even at rc 0, so `final.passed == final.total` can coexist with a full `newly_failing` list, contradicting the fallback rule at `:86-88`. (Dissent DISS-003, DISS-C-003 — confirmed.)
**Suggestion:** Derive `newly` from the fallback ids when both runs are fallback (`rf["rc"] != 0` → all of `base_ok`, else none) and expose `regressions.parse_error` so consumers can exclude the row.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:652-653` — `all_pass` ignores `rc` and `timed_out`. A suite that prints its complete summary and then hangs (rc 124) or crashes in teardown is green for `verdict_accuracy_per_gate`, `suite_green_*` and the self-checks; conversely nothing cross-checks rc against the parsed line, so agent-authored code imported by the hidden tests (a new root `conftest.py` the fixture lacks is not restored by `prepare`, `:657-674`) can print a forged `N passed in 0.1s` and `os._exit(0)`. (Dissent DISS-002, DISS-C-002 — confirmed as a gap; exploit requires a gaming agent.)
**Suggestion:** Treat `rc != 0` with a clean summary, or `rc == 0` with failures, as `parse_error: true`; require `not timed_out` in `all_pass`; consider removing `conftest.py` / `pytest.ini` / `pyproject.toml` / `setup.cfg` / `tox.ini` not present in the fixture before running.

### 3. Contamination false positives

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:964` — `"hidden" in low` fires on `rg --hidden`, `fd --hidden`, a Grep pattern such as `display: hidden`, or any CSS/HTML edit; `ABS_WORD` (`:977-980`) treats a quoted route string like `grep -rn "/api/users" src/` as a filesystem path, and `/home`, `/root`, `/mnt`, `/srv` are outside the container allow-list (`:949`), so `ls /home` is `outside_path`. The first hit short-circuits (`:1034`), so one benign hit marks the run contaminated and downstream aggregation drops it. The header calls the scan a lower bound on leakage; it is also an unbounded source of false flags. (Dissent DISS-C-001 — confirmed.)
**Suggestion:** Match `hidden` as a path component (`(^|/)hidden(/|$)`) on path fields and path-shaped Bash words; record every hit in a `contamination_hits` list and keep `contaminated` as the first.

# Audit Rubrics

Structured evaluation rubrics for each audit category. Use these to score findings consistently.

## How to Use

1. For each dimension, assess the codebase against the criteria
2. Assign score 1-5 based on the rubric
3. Record reasoning trace explaining the score
4. Calculate category average for overall health

---

## Security Rubrics

### SEC-IV: Input Validation
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | All inputs validated, sanitized, and typed. Allowlist approach used. Schema validation on APIs. |
| 4 | Most inputs validated with minor gaps. Edge cases may lack validation. |
| 3 | Basic validation present but incomplete. Some injection risks remain. |
| 2 | Minimal validation. Clear injection vulnerabilities exist. |
| 1 | No input validation. User input flows directly to sensitive operations. |

### SEC-AZ: Authorization
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | RBAC/ABAC properly implemented. All routes protected. Least privilege enforced. |
| 4 | Authorization present with minor gaps (some routes missing checks). |
| 3 | Basic auth checks but inconsistent. Privilege escalation may be possible. |
| 2 | Weak authorization. Easy bypass or missing on critical routes. |
| 1 | No authorization or completely broken access control. |

### SEC-CI: Confidentiality/Integrity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Encryption at rest and in transit. Proper key management. Data classified and protected. |
| 4 | Good encryption with minor gaps. Some sensitive data handling could improve. |
| 3 | Basic encryption but inconsistent. Some data exposure risks. |
| 2 | Weak or missing encryption. Sensitive data partially exposed. |
| 1 | No encryption. Sensitive data in plaintext. Secrets in code. |

### SEC-IN: Injection Prevention
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Parameterized queries everywhere. No string concatenation in queries. ORM used safely. |
| 4 | Mostly safe with minor gaps in edge cases. |
| 3 | Mixed usage. Some queries parameterized, others vulnerable. |
| 2 | Frequent string concatenation in queries. Clear SQL/NoSQL injection paths. |
| 1 | Pervasive injection vulnerabilities. Eval/exec with user input. |

### SEC-AV: Availability/Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Rate limiting, circuit breakers, graceful degradation. DoS protection in place. |
| 4 | Good availability measures with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic rate limiting but incomplete. Some DoS vectors remain. |
| 2 | Minimal protection. Resource exhaustion possible. |
| 1 | No availability protection. Trivial DoS attacks possible. |

---

## Architecture Rubrics

### ARCH-MO: Modularity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Clear separation of concerns. Well-defined interfaces. Easy to modify/extend. |
| 4 | Good modularity with minor coupling issues. |
| 3 | Some modularity but tight coupling in places. |
| 2 | Poor separation. Components heavily interdependent. |
| 1 | Monolithic. No clear boundaries. |

### ARCH-SC: Scalability
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Horizontally scalable. Stateless services. Caching strategy. Database sharding ready. |
| 4 | Mostly scalable with minor bottlenecks. |
| 3 | Can scale vertically but horizontal scaling problematic. |
| 2 | Scalability issues. Single points of failure. |
| 1 | Cannot scale. Architecture prevents growth. |

### ARCH-RE: Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Fault tolerant. Graceful degradation. Retry logic. Health checks. Circuit breakers. |
| 4 | Good resilience with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic error handling but cascading failures possible. |
| 2 | Fragile. Single component failure affects system. |
| 1 | No resilience. Any failure brings down system. |

### ARCH-CX: Complexity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Simple, elegant design. Easy to understand. Well-documented patterns. |
| 4 | Reasonable complexity with minor over-engineering. |

# auditing-security — Security Dissenter (Phase 1C) detail

SKILL.md Phase 1C names the gate, the hook, the override and the invocation. This file carries
the merge rules and the failed-run record.

## Independence

The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.

## Merging dissenter findings into Phase 2

1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

## Failed or unavailable dissenter

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.
- **`workdir_unavailable`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed`** (the range's `git diff` failed — e.g. a base ref a shallow clone lacks; `workdir_unavailable` with `metadata.path` is a previous round's file that could not be moved aside — make the a2a directory writable; written BEFORE the run lock, or with it released; non-zero exit, stdout only; nothing moved aside, so any envelope at the path is the PREVIOUS run's and never this round's evidence) — record it: `--record-fallback <the status> --reason "<its stdout line>" --since <the run started time>` (it never displaces an envelope written after that) moves that envelope and its `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` sidecars aside as `<name>.prev` (as a run does at start) before it writes, so `verdict-derive.sh` judges this round's record, not the last round's.

A record names what it moved aside (`metadata.displaced`: status, timestamp, findings, rejected); `verdict-derive.sh` warns when that held findings. `verdict-derive.sh` never scans `.prev` files (they are the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback) and reports `.prev` files with NO envelope as a `dissent_aborted` violation, which a fallback record clears; `rejected_sidecars: []` does not silence a canonical `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` beside it — that is this run's own partial work, counted whether listed or not: triage its rows under `## Rejected dissent payloads`.

# Audit Rubrics

Structured evaluation rubrics for each audit category. Use these to score findings consistently.

## How to Use

1. For each dimension, assess the codebase against the criteria
2. Assign score 1-5 based on the rubric
3. Record reasoning trace explaining the score
4. Calculate category average for overall health

---

## Security Rubrics

### SEC-IV: Input Validation
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | All inputs validated, sanitized, and typed. Allowlist approach used. Schema validation on APIs. |
| 4 | Most inputs validated with minor gaps. Edge cases may lack validation. |
| 3 | Basic validation present but incomplete. Some injection risks remain. |
| 2 | Minimal validation. Clear injection vulnerabilities exist. |
| 1 | No input validation. User input flows directly to sensitive operations. |

### SEC-AZ: Authorization
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | RBAC/ABAC properly implemented. All routes protected. Least privilege enforced. |
| 4 | Authorization present with minor gaps (some routes missing checks). |
| 3 | Basic auth checks but inconsistent. Privilege escalation may be possible. |
| 2 | Weak authorization. Easy bypass or missing on critical routes. |
| 1 | No authorization or completely broken access control. |

### SEC-CI: Confidentiality/Integrity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Encryption at rest and in transit. Proper key management. Data classified and protected. |
| 4 | Good encryption with minor gaps. Some sensitive data handling could improve. |
| 3 | Basic encryption but inconsistent. Some data exposure risks. |
| 2 | Weak or missing encryption. Sensitive data partially exposed. |
| 1 | No encryption. Sensitive data in plaintext. Secrets in code. |

### SEC-IN: Injection Prevention
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Parameterized queries everywhere. No string concatenation in queries. ORM used safely. |
| 4 | Mostly safe with minor gaps in edge cases. |
| 3 | Mixed usage. Some queries parameterized, others vulnerable. |
| 2 | Frequent string concatenation in queries. Clear SQL/NoSQL injection paths. |
| 1 | Pervasive injection vulnerabilities. Eval/exec with user input. |

### SEC-AV: Availability/Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Rate limiting, circuit breakers, graceful degradation. DoS protection in place. |
| 4 | Good availability measures with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic rate limiting but incomplete. Some DoS vectors remain. |
| 2 | Minimal protection. Resource exhaustion possible. |
| 1 | No availability protection. Trivial DoS attacks possible. |

---

## Architecture Rubrics

### ARCH-MO: Modularity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Clear separation of concerns. Well-defined interfaces. Easy to modify/extend. |
| 4 | Good modularity with minor coupling issues. |
| 3 | Some modularity but tight coupling in places. |
| 2 | Poor separation. Components heavily interdependent. |
| 1 | Monolithic. No clear boundaries. |

### ARCH-SC: Scalability
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Horizontally scalable. Stateless services. Caching strategy. Database sharding ready. |
| 4 | Mostly scalable with minor bottlenecks. |
| 3 | Can scale vertically but horizontal scaling problematic. |
| 2 | Scalability issues. Single points of failure. |
| 1 | Cannot scale. Architecture prevents growth. |

### ARCH-RE: Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Fault tolerant. Graceful degradation. Retry logic. Health checks. Circuit breakers. |
| 4 | Good resilience with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic error handling but cascading failures possible. |
| 2 | Fragile. Single component failure affects system. |
| 1 | No resilience. Any failure brings down system. |

### ARCH-CX: Complexity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Simple, elegant design. Easy to understand. Well-documented patterns. |
| 4 | Reasonable complexity with minor over-engineering. |
| 3 | Moderately complex. Learning curve for new developers. |
| 2 | Overly complex. Hard to reason about. |

## Independence

The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.

## Merging dissenter findings into Phase 2

1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

## Failed or unavailable dissenter

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.
- **`workdir_unavailable`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed`** (the range's `git diff` failed — e.g. a base ref a shallow clone lacks; `workdir_unavailable` with `metadata.path` is a previous round's file that could not be moved aside — make the a2a directory writable; written BEFORE the run lock, or with it released; non-zero exit, stdout only; nothing moved aside, so any envelope at the path is the PREVIOUS run's and never this round's evidence) — record it: `--record-fallback <the status> --reason "<its stdout line>" --since <the run started time>` (it never displaces an envelope written after that) moves that envelope and its `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` sidecars aside as `<name>.prev` (as a run does at start) before it writes, so `verdict-derive.sh` judges this round's record, not the last round's.

A record names what it moved aside (`metadata.displaced`: status, timestamp, findings, rejected); `verdict-derive.sh` warns when that held findings. `verdict-derive.sh` never scans `.prev` files (they are the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback) and reports `.prev` files with NO envelope as a `dissent_aborted` violation, which a fallback record clears; `rejected_sidecars: []` does not silence a canonical `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` beside it — that is this run's own partial work, counted whether listed or not: triage its rows under `## Rejected dissent payloads`.

Then set a `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker in the audit report. Empty
findings from a run that completed are a normal pass, not a degraded review.

A bare `planned: false` (the block opted out, `companion_voice: false`) is the operator's choice, not a degradation.
Otherwise a completed run is still a degraded audit when its second voice is missing: `companion_voice.status` `failed`
or `fold_failed`, `counted_as` `duplicate_voice` or `sole_voice`, or `planned: false` WITH a `reason` (a companion that
never started: `no_workdir`, `no_route`, `prompt_copy_failed`) — set the `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker and name the
reason. On a host with no route to the other family at all (`no_route`: no key and no CLI for it) that marker is set on
every audit; `companion_voice: false` on the block is the operator's way to say one voice is the host's shape.

## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)

**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated

succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a

When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.
- **`workdir_unavailable`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed`** (the range's `git diff` failed — e.g. a base ref a shallow clone lacks; `workdir_unavailable` with `metadata.path` is a previous round's file that could not be moved aside — make the a2a directory writable; written BEFORE the run lock, or with it released; non-zero exit, stdout only; nothing moved aside, so any envelope at the path is the PREVIOUS run's and never this round's evidence) — record it: `--record-fallback <the status> --reason "<its stdout line>" --since <the run started time>` (it never displaces an envelope written after that) moves that envelope and its `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` sidecars aside as `<name>.prev` (as a run does at start) before it writes, so `verdict-derive.sh` judges this round's record, not the last round's.

A record names what it moved aside (`metadata.displaced`: status, timestamp, findings, rejected); `verdict-derive.sh` warns when that held findings. `verdict-derive.sh` never scans `.prev` files (they are the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback) and reports `.prev` files with NO envelope as a `dissent_aborted` violation, which a fallback record clears; `rejected_sidecars: []` does not silence a canonical `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` beside it — that is this run's own partial work, counted whether listed or not: triage its rows under `## Rejected dissent payloads`.

Then set a `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker in the audit report. Empty
findings from a run that completed are a normal pass, not a degraded review.

A bare `planned: false` (the block opted out, `companion_voice: false`) is the operator's choice, not a degradation.
Otherwise a completed run is still a degraded audit when its second voice is missing: `companion_voice.status` `failed`
or `fold_failed`, `counted_as` `duplicate_voice` or `sole_voice`, or `planned: false` WITH a `reason` (a companion that
never started: `no_workdir`, `no_route`, `prompt_copy_failed`) — set the `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker and name the
reason. On a host with no route to the other family at all (`no_route`: no key and no CLI for it) that marker is set on
every audit; `companion_voice: false` on the block is the operator's way to say one voice is the host's shape.

## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)

**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated
(`verdict_quality.voices_succeeded_ids` lists only completed voices). `companion_voice.status` is `succeeded`,
`failed` or `fold_failed`; `verdict_quality.voices_planned` counts the aggregated envelopes — 2 whenever the companion ran,
completed or not (a failed one is listed in `voices_dropped`) — except a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's
succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a
dropped entry naming the model the companion answered with is removed (INV-5). `companion_voice.counted_as`
(`independent_voice`, `duplicate_voice`, `sole_voice` — the primary never answered) names the outcome, and `planned: false` with a `reason` (`no_workdir`, `no_route`,
`prompt_copy_failed`) is a companion that never started; a bare `planned: false` is the opt-out. The
companion's findings arrive re-numbered `DISS-C-NNN` with a `voice` field; the primary's carry
`voice` too. `metadata.companion_voice` records `{planned, family, family_basis, chain, model,
status: succeeded|failed|fold_failed, failure_class: auth|model_unavailable|quota|timeout|lock_wait|malformed|null,
cost_cents, attempts}`; a companion whose chain fails is a dropped voice (degraded for an audit,
never blocking a review). Opt-out per block: `flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice: false`
(the YAML boolean spellings in any case; a value that is none of them is reported and the voice stays on).

**Tolerant schema (D-2.2).** A finding missing only `failure_mode` is no longer dropped: the
first sentence of its `description` (≤ 200 chars) becomes `failure_mode` and the finding is
marked `failure_mode_derived: true` (a missing `id` is filled positionally, `id_derived: true`).
Severity, category and description are never touched. Payloads that still fail go to the
sidecar (`adversarial-rejected-<type>.jsonl`, `-companion` suffix for the second voice) **and**
to `metadata.rejected_summary[]` as `{index, severity, title, title_derived, anchor, reason, description_head}`.

**The contract (D-2.3).** When `rejected_summary` is non-empty the feedback file MUST contain a
`## Rejected dissent payloads` section with one line per entry — `- <title> (<severity>, <anchor>)
— <reason>: triaged as <real defect → counted under the matching heading | not a defect → why>`.
`verdict-derive.sh` reads the sibling envelope (`adversarial-<gate>.json`, or `--envelope <path>`)
and marks the trailer INCONSISTENT (exit 1) when the section is missing. Reading a sidecar row:
`payload` is the model's finding as normalised, `reject_reason` the clause it failed, and
`repair_attempted` / `repair_succeeded` whether the bounded repair round-trip ran.

**Round-1 hardening (sprint-248 review, sixteen live two-voice runs).** One list, by envelope field; both skills' copies of
this block are kept byte-identical (CMP-138 fails on any drift).

- **Two voices, one envelope.** The companion runs in its own sub-workdir with a log and its own copies of the prompt files.
  The envelope's `cost_usd` / tokens are BOTH voices; the per-voice spend stays under `companion_voice.cost_cents`, and
  `budget_cents` is a per-voice cap (a malformed cap is 0 cents — the run fails closed with `status: budget_exceeded`).
  Findings carry `voice` (the outer hop, matching `final_model`) and `answered_by` (the model that produced them);
  `companion_voice.answered_by` is the companion's own succeeded id. An operator may set
  `flatline_protocol.<block>.companion_chain: {anthropic: [...], openai: [...]}` to replace the default chains of D-2.1
  (used as given; only those two keys are read — keyed by the companion's family). A family with neither a credential nor its CLI on PATH is `reason: no_route`; a prompt copy that fails
  is `reason: prompt_copy_failed` (no fork). `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_KEEP_WORKDIR=1` keeps the `/tmp` workdir's files, never a
  process.
- **`companion_voice.independent` / `counted_as`.** Independence compares the two `answered_by` families (the primary's
  succeeded id, not its configured hop). Same family — or either family `unknown`, an id no catalog entry or name rule
  places, which is no evidence of a second family: the companion's findings are kept (tagged) but its envelope
  contributes no voice to verdict quality — `counted_as: duplicate_voice` (the aggregator counts distinct voices; its
  INV-5 forbids one id both succeeded and dropped, so a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's succeeded voices
