     3	# ablation-grade.sh — the cycle-130 ablation grader (SDD §3.6, §5.7, D-4.7, D-4.8;
     4	# PRD FR-6 AC-6.1/6.2/6.4; DEC-0401, DEC-0413, DEC-0414, DEC-0420, DEC-0491, DEC-0493)
     5	#
     6	# Grades ONE run directory written by pipeline-run.sh against its task and writes
     7	# grade.json (the input ablation-row.sh joins into the runs.jsonl row), or
     8	# self-checks a task (--self-check) on a synthetic run built from the task itself.
     9	#
    10	# Usage:
    11	#   ablation-grade.sh <run-dir> <task-id> [--suite-root DIR] [--tasks-dir tasks|smoke]
    12	#                     [--out FILE] [--json] [--executor container|host]
    13	#                     [--image loa-ablation:258] [--docker-bin D]
    14	#                     [--allow-unfrozen] [--allow-partial]
    15	#   ablation-grade.sh --self-check base|reference|noisy --task-yaml F [--suite-root DIR]
    16	#                     [--executor …] [--image …] [--docker-bin D] [--json]
    17	#                     [--allow-unfrozen] [--allow-partial]
    18	#
    19	# Options:
    20	#   --suite-root DIR   suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0; with
    21	#                      --self-check, the directory two levels above the task dir)
    22	#   --tasks-dir T      tasks (default) or smoke: the task is <root>/<T>/<task-id>/
    23	#   --out FILE         where grade.json goes (default <run-dir>/grade.json)
    24	#   --json             also print grade.json (self-check: the verdict object) on stdout
    25	#   --executor MODE    container (default; DEC-0491) or host
    26	#   --image IMG        the grading image (default loa-ablation:258)
    27	#   --docker-bin D     docker CLI (default $EVAL_DOCKER_BIN, else docker)
    28	#   --allow-unfrozen   grade although freeze.sh --check fails or the suite has no
    29	#                      MANIFEST.sha256 yet (task authoring only); grade.json records
    30	#                      suite_frozen: false. Without it a drift is exit 2 (DEC-0414).
    31	#   --allow-partial    passed to freeze.sh --check (fewer than four tasks per type)
    32	#   --self-check MODE  base | reference | noisy (noisy: review-catch only), see below
    33	#   --task-yaml F      the task to self-check (<root>/<tasks|smoke>/<id>/task.yaml)
    34	#
    35	# Reads ONLY (DEC-0413): <run-dir>/sandbox/, <run-dir>/snapshots/{index.json,<LABEL>.bundle},
    36	# <run-dir>/transcripts/events-*.jsonl, <run-dir>/eval/adversarial-{review,audit}.json,
    37	# the task's directory under the suite root (task.yaml, hidden/, fixture/), the suite's
    38	# MANIFEST.sha256 (through freeze.sh) and, for review-catch, the key manifest the task
    39	# names (review_catch.manifest) and its PR fixture (self-check only). It never reads
    40	# <run-dir>/meta/, the batch MANIFEST.json, or the sandbox copies of the dissent
    41	# envelopes (tamperable; the harness copies under eval/ are authoritative). It writes
    42	# only <run-dir>/grading/ and the --out file; nothing under sandbox/ is ever written.
    43	#
    44	# Freeze: freeze.sh --check --root <suite-root> runs first (with --smoke when the
    45	# suite manifest lists smoke/ paths, so a manifest frozen with --smoke checks as it
    46	# was frozen); a drift or a missing manifest refuses the grade (exit 2) unless
    47	# --allow-unfrozen.
    48	#
    49	# Grading trees (D-4.8) under <run-dir>/grading/<label>/, recreated on every call:
    50	#   final      sandbox/ as the agent left it, minus the top-level .git .claude CLAUDE.md
    51	#              .loa.config.yaml grimoires .run .beads .eval pr, every __pycache__ and
    52	#              .pytest_cache, and anything that is not a regular file, directory or
    53	#              symlink (a FIFO never blocks the copy)
    54	#   implement  the IMPLEMENT snapshot (snapshots/IMPLEMENT.bundle, commit
    55	#              index.json.implement): the tree REVIEW read; graded when REVIEW ran or
    56	#              when AUDIT ran without a fix1 snapshot
    57	#   fix1       the FIX1 snapshot: the tree AUDIT read; graded when AUDIT ran
    58	#   base       the task fixture: the baseline for regression_command (and, refactor,
    59	#              the suite-green-at-base check)
    60	# A snapshot is extracted with `git bundle unbundle` into a scratch bare repository and
    61	# `git archive <commit>` (a member that would land outside the tree is skipped). In
    62	# every tree each grader_protected path is restored from the fixture (a deleted file is
    63	# recreated, a modified one overwritten, a path the fixture lacks is removed; a
    64	# symlinked parent is replaced by a directory), then every hidden/manifest.json entry
    65	# is written at its dest (a same-named file is overwritten, a deleted directory
    66	# recreated). Churn (diff_lines, files_changed) compares the final tree against the
    67	# fixture before any restore: added + removed lines per changed text file (difflib),
    68	# every added, removed or modified file counted once; null for review-catch.
    69	#
    70	# Commands run INSIDE the image (DEC-0491):
    71	#   docker run --rm --network none --read-only --tmpfs /tmp:rw,size=256m --user <uid>:<gid>
    72	#     -v <tree>:/workspace:rw -w /workspace -e HOME=/tmp -e LC_ALL=C -e TMPDIR=/tmp
    73	#     <image> timeout 120 <cmd…>
    74	# `python3 -m pytest …` (or `pytest …`) becomes `python3 -I -s -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider
    75	# -q --rootdir /workspace -rA …` (one -q: -qq would drop the summary line; -rA lists every
    76	# outcome, from which the ids come); `bats …` becomes `bats --tap …` with BATS_LIB_PATH
    77	# unset (the -e set is the whole container environment). --executor host runs the same
    78	# argv in the tree under `env -i PATH HOME=<scratch> LC_ALL=C TMPDIR=<scratch>
    79	# PYTHONUSERBASE=<the caller's user base>` with pytest as `python3 -P -m pytest …`:
    80	# no -I or -s on the host, because the host's pytest lives in the user site (the Sprint
    81	# 258 smoke found no pytest under `-I -s`); PYTHONUSERBASE is passed for the same reason.
    82	#
    83	# Parsing: the pytest summary line (`N passed, M failed, K error …`) or TAP (`1..N`,
    84	# `ok`/`not ok`). A collection error is expanded to the test functions of its file; the
    85	# hidden total is never below the static case count of the hidden test files (`def test`
    86	# / `@test`). A command without a parseable summary counts total = that static count
    87	# (at least 1), passed = 0 when it exited non-zero (total when it exited 0), with
    88	# parse_error: true. Ids: "t<k>", k = the 1-based position of the case in file order
    89	# (pytest: path, then the line of its def; TAP: the test number); regression ids are
    90	# positions in the base run, newly_failing = failing at final, passing at base.
    91	#
    92	# Review-catch (DEC-0420): grading/gates-combined.md is the arm-neutral reduction: every
    93	# `path:line[-line]` citation (parser of recall-vs-defects.sh 1.1.2; the LOA-VERDICT
    94	# trailer removed first) from sandbox/review.md (the A0 contract),
    95	# sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/{engineer-feedback.md,auditor-sprint-feedback.md}
    96	# and each finding's anchor (and file:line) in eval/adversarial-{review,audit}.json,
    97	# one normalised `path:line[-line]` line each (pr/head/ → head/, a/ b/ and /workspace/
    98	# prefixes dropped), duplicates dropped. recall-vs-defects.sh <grading-dir> <pr-NN>
    99	# gates-combined.md (EVAL_MANIFEST_DIR = the manifest's directory) gives recall;
   100	# flags = its findings_cited; missed = defect positions ("d2"), never defect ids.
   101	# false_positives = citations within ±3 of no anchor, deduplicated by cited region
   102	# (same file, overlapping ±3 windows count once).
   103	#
   104	# Verdicts: the last `<!-- LOA-VERDICT {…} -->` trailer of engineer-feedback.md (review)
   105	# and auditor-sprint-feedback.md (audit); a gate ran when its feedback file exists.
   106	# verdict = {source_file, value}: the audit's, else the review's, else review.md's
   107	# `Verdict:` line (A0), else null. verdict_accuracy_per_gate {review, audit}: build —
   108	# true when APPROVED and the tree that gate read passes every hidden test, or
   109	# CHANGES_REQUIRED and it fails one; review-catch — true iff (CHANGES_REQUIRED) ==
   110	# (the key holds a high or critical defect); a gate without a trailer is false; a gate
   111	# that did not run is null. verdict_accuracy = audit's, else review's, else null.
   112	#
   113	# Contamination (D-4.7, DEC-0493): every tool_use input in transcripts/events-*.jsonl —
   114	# Bash command; Read/Grep/Glob file_path|path|pattern; Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit
   115	# file_path|notebook_path; WebFetch url; WebSearch query — is checked for: `hidden` (any
   116	# case) → hidden; grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0 → suite_path; 0xHoneyJar/loa →
   117	# repo_name; `git log … --all` or `git reflog` (Bash) → git_history; an absolute path
   118	# (path fields, the Glob pattern, path-shaped Bash words; a one-component `/x/` word
   119	# is read as a regex) outside /workspace /tmp /home/evaluser /dev /proc /sys /usr /bin
   120	# /sbin /lib /lib64 /etc /opt /var (container), or outside the sandbox root (the
   121	# sessions' init cwd and <run-dir>/sandbox), /tmp, those system directories and the
   122	# caller's ~/.claude ~/.claude.json ~/.codex ~/.aws (host) → outside_path. The first hit
   123	# in phase order is contaminated: {phase, pattern, excerpt_id: "<phase>:<line>"} (never
   124	# the text); else null. The scan is a LOWER BOUND on leakage: obfuscated access, reads
   125	# by programs the agent wrote, and network access by other means are not seen.
   126	#
   127	# grade.json (ids only in every summary field: no test name, defect title or excerpt):
   128	#   {schema_version: 1, grader_version: "1.0.0", task_id, task_type, suite_frozen,
   129	#    executor_mode, image, snapshots_graded: [labels], hidden_tests {passed, total,
   130	#    failed_names, parse_error, timed_out}, structural (refactor: {passed, total,
   131	#    failed_names, parse_error, suite_green_base, suite_green_final}; else null),
   132	#    regressions ({newly_failing, base {passed, total}, final {passed, total}} or null
   133	#    without regression_command), snapshot_tests {implement?, fix1?: {passed, total}},
   134	#    recall (review-catch {defects_seeded, defects_caught, recall, flags, missed}; else
   135	#    null), false_positives, verdict, verdicts {review, audit}, verdict_accuracy,
   136	#    verdict_accuracy_per_gate {review, audit}, diff_lines, files_changed, contaminated}
   137	# No timestamp and no scratch path is written: the same run grades byte-identically.
   138	#
   139	# Self-check (DEC-0401; AC-2.3): a synthetic run under mktemp -d built from the task.
   140	#   base       build: the fixture is the final tree → PASS when at least one hidden test
   141	#              fails and the fixture suite (regression_command, when set) is green;
   142	#              refactor: structural check red and suite green; review-catch: an empty
   143	#              findings file → recall 0.0
   144	#   reference  build: the fixture with hidden/reference.patch (patch -p1) → every hidden
   145	#              test passes, suite green; refactor: structural green, suite green;
   146	#              review-catch: a findings file citing every key anchor → recall 1.0
   147	#   noisy      review-catch: every line of every pr/head/ file cited → false_positives
   148	#              greater than the reference findings file's
   149	# Prints `self-check <mode> <task-id>: PASS|FAIL <evidence>`.
   150	#
   151	# Exit codes: 0 graded / self-check PASS; 1 self-check FAIL; 2 error (usage, missing run
   152	# dir, task not found, unfrozen suite without --allow-unfrozen, docker or the image
   153	# missing in container mode, a tool failure).
   154	#
   155	# Tested by evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats (docker = evals/tests/fixtures/docker-stub.sh).
   156	# No .claude/ code is sourced and nothing is sourced or eval'd from a variable (eval.yml
   157	# trust boundary); hashing is Python hashlib.
   158	# =============================================================================
   159	set -euo pipefail
   160	export LC_ALL=C
   161	
   162	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
   163	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
   164	case "${1:-}" in -h|--help) sed -n '3,/^# =====/p' "$0" | sed '$d' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;; esac
   165	
   166	exec python3 -I - "$SCRIPT_DIR" "$REPO_ROOT" "${EVAL_DOCKER_BIN:-docker}" "$@" <<'PY'
   167	import argparse, difflib, json, os, re, shutil, site, stat, subprocess, sys, tarfile, tempfile
   168	
   169	GRADER_VERSION = "1.0.0"
   170	SCRIPT_DIR, REPO_ROOT, DOCKER_DEFAULT = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
   171	SPRINT = "sprint-1"
   172	TEST_TIMEOUT_S = 120
   173	EXCLUDE_TOP = {".git", ".claude", "CLAUDE.md", ".loa.config.yaml", "grimoires", ".run", ".beads", ".eval", "pr"}
   174	EXCLUDE_ANY = {"__pycache__", ".pytest_cache"}
   175	PHASE_ORDER = ["PLAN", "BARE", "IMPLEMENT", "REVIEW", "FIX1", "AUDIT", "FIX2"]
   176	
   177	
   178	class GradeError(Exception):
   179	    pass
   180	
   181	
   182	def die(msg):
   183	    print(f"ablation-grade: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
   184	    sys.exit(2)
   185	
   186	
   187	ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="ablation-grade.sh", add_help=False)
   188	ap.add_argument("run_dir", nargs="?")
   189	ap.add_argument("task_id", nargs="?")
   190	ap.add_argument("--suite-root")
   191	ap.add_argument("--tasks-dir", choices=["tasks", "smoke"])
   192	ap.add_argument("--out")
   193	ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
   194	ap.add_argument("--executor", choices=["container", "host"], default="container")
   195	ap.add_argument("--image", default="loa-ablation:258")
   196	ap.add_argument("--docker-bin", default=DOCKER_DEFAULT)
   197	ap.add_argument("--allow-unfrozen", action="store_true")
   198	ap.add_argument("--allow-partial", action="store_true")
   199	ap.add_argument("--self-check", choices=["base", "reference", "noisy"])
   200	ap.add_argument("--task-yaml")
   201	try:
   202	    A = ap.parse_args(sys.argv[4:])
   203	except SystemExit:
   204	    sys.exit(2)
   205	
   206	
   207	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ small helpers
   208	def run(cmd, **kw):
   209	    return subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, **kw)
   210	
   211	
   212	def load_yaml(path):
   213	    p = run(["yq", "-o=json", ".", path])
   214	    if p.returncode != 0:
   215	        raise GradeError(f"task yaml does not parse: {path}")
   216	    try:
   217	        return json.loads(p.stdout)
   218	    except ValueError:
   219	        raise GradeError(f"task yaml does not parse: {path}")
   220	
   221	
   222	def read_json(path):
   223	    try:
   224	        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   225	            return json.load(f)
   226	    except (OSError, ValueError):
   227	        return None
   228	
   229	
   230	def is_within(path, root):
   231	    path, root = os.path.realpath(path), os.path.realpath(root)
   232	    return path == root or path.startswith(root + os.sep)
   233	
   234	
   235	def remove_path(p):
   236	    if os.path.islink(p) or os.path.isfile(p):
   237	        os.unlink(p)
   238	    elif os.path.isdir(p):
   239	        for r, ds, _fs in os.walk(p):
   240	            for d in ds:
   241	                try:
   242	                    os.chmod(os.path.join(r, d), 0o700)
   243	                except OSError:
   244	                    pass
   245	        shutil.rmtree(p)
   246	    elif os.path.lexists(p):
   247	        os.unlink(p)
   248	
   249	
   250	def safe_rel(rel):
   251	    if not isinstance(rel, str) or not rel or rel.startswith("/") or "\\" in rel:
   252	        return None
   253	    parts = [x for x in rel.split("/") if x not in ("", ".")]
   254	    if not parts or ".." in parts:
   255	        return None
   256	    return parts
   257	
   258	
   259	def ensure_parent(tree, parts):
   260	    """make every parent component of tree/parts a real directory inside tree"""
   261	    cur = tree
   262	    for comp in parts[:-1]:
   263	        cur = os.path.join(cur, comp)
   264	        if os.path.islink(cur) or (os.path.lexists(cur) and not os.path.isdir(cur)):
   265	            os.unlink(cur)
   266	        if not os.path.isdir(cur):
   267	            os.mkdir(cur)
   268	    return os.path.join(cur, parts[-1])
   269	
   270	
   271	def copy_tree(src, dst, top_exclude=frozenset()):
   272	    """regular files, directories and symlinks only; caches dropped"""
   273	    os.makedirs(dst, exist_ok=True)
   274	    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(src, followlinks=False):
   275	        rel = os.path.relpath(root, src)
   276	        keep = []
   277	        for d in sorted(dirs):
   278	            if (rel == "." and d in top_exclude) or d in EXCLUDE_ANY:
   279	                continue
   280	            sp = os.path.join(root, d)
   281	            dp = os.path.join(dst, rel, d)
   282	            if os.path.islink(sp):
   283	                os.symlink(os.readlink(sp), dp)
   284	                continue
   285	            os.makedirs(dp, exist_ok=True)
   286	            keep.append(d)
   287	        dirs[:] = keep
   288	        for f in sorted(files):
   289	            if rel == "." and f in top_exclude:
   290	                continue
   291	            sp, dp = os.path.join(root, f), os.path.join(dst, rel, f)
   292	            st = os.lstat(sp)
   293	            if stat.S_ISLNK(st.st_mode):
   294	                os.symlink(os.readlink(sp), dp)
   295	            elif stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
   296	                shutil.copyfile(sp, dp)
   297	                os.chmod(dp, (st.st_mode & 0o777) | 0o600)
   298	
   299	
   300	def put_file(tree, rel, src):
   301	    parts = safe_rel(rel)
   302	    if parts is None:
   303	        raise GradeError(f"unsafe path: {rel!r}")
   304	    dst = ensure_parent(tree, parts)
   305	    if os.path.lexists(dst):
   306	        remove_path(dst)
   307	    if os.path.isdir(src) and not os.path.islink(src):
   308	        copy_tree(src, dst)
   309	    else:
   310	        shutil.copyfile(src, dst)
   311	        os.chmod(dst, (os.stat(src).st_mode & 0o777) | 0o600)
   312	
   313	
   314	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ task loading
   315	class Task:
   316	    pass
   317	
   318	
   319	def load_task(task_yaml, suite_root):
   320	    t = Task()
   321	    t.yaml = os.path.abspath(task_yaml)
   322	    t.dir = os.path.dirname(t.yaml)
   323	    t.suite_root = os.path.abspath(suite_root)
   324	    t.spec = load_yaml(t.yaml)
   325	    if not isinstance(t.spec, dict):
   326	        raise GradeError(f"task yaml is not a mapping: {task_yaml}")
   327	    t.id = t.spec.get("id") or ""
   328	    t.type = t.spec.get("type") or ""
   329	    if t.type not in ("bug-fix", "feature-build", "refactor", "review-catch"):
   330	        raise GradeError(f"unknown task type: {t.type!r}")

    55	#              index.json.implement): the tree REVIEW read; graded when REVIEW ran or
    56	#              when AUDIT ran without a fix1 snapshot

    58	#   base       the task fixture: the baseline for regression_command (and, refactor,
    59	#              the suite-green-at-base check)
    60	# A snapshot is extracted with `git bundle unbundle` into a scratch bare repository and
    61	# `git archive <commit>` (a member that would land outside the tree is skipped). In
    62	# every tree each grader_protected path is restored from the fixture (a deleted file is
    63	# recreated, a modified one overwritten, a path the fixture lacks is removed; a
    64	# symlinked parent is replaced by a directory), then every hidden/manifest.json entry
    65	# is written at its dest (a same-named file is overwritten, a deleted directory
    66	# recreated). Churn (diff_lines, files_changed) compares the final tree against the
    67	# fixture before any restore: added + removed lines per changed text file (difflib),
    68	# every added, removed or modified file counted once; null for review-catch.
    69	#
    70	# Commands run INSIDE the image (DEC-0491):
    71	#   docker run --rm --network none --read-only --tmpfs /tmp:rw,size=256m --user <uid>:<gid>
    72	#     -v <tree>:/workspace:rw -w /workspace -e HOME=/tmp -e LC_ALL=C -e TMPDIR=/tmp
    73	#     <image> timeout 120 <cmd…>

    75	# -q --rootdir /workspace -rA …` (one -q: -qq would drop the summary line; -rA lists every
    76	# outcome, from which the ids come); `bats …` becomes `bats --tap …` with BATS_LIB_PATH
    77	# unset (the -e set is the whole container environment). --executor host runs the same
    78	# argv in the tree under `env -i PATH HOME=<scratch> LC_ALL=C TMPDIR=<scratch>

    80	# no -I or -s on the host, because the host's pytest lives in the user site (the Sprint
    81	# 258 smoke found no pytest under `-I -s`); PYTHONUSERBASE is passed for the same reason.

600	def parse_tap(out):
601	    plan, seen = None, {}
602	    for l in out.splitlines():
603	        m = re.match(r"^1\.\.(\d+)", l)
604	        if m and plan is None:
605	            plan = int(m.group(1))

608	        if m:
609	            n = int(m.group(2))
610	            desc = re.sub(r"\s+#\s*(?:skip|SKIP|todo|TODO).*$", "", m.group(3)).strip()
611	            seen[n] = (m.group(1) is None, desc or f"#{n}")
612	    if plan is None and not seen:
613	        return None
614	    total = plan if plan is not None else len(seen)
615	    if total == 0:
616	        return None
617	    nums = sorted(set(range(1, total + 1)) | set(seen))
618	    names = {n: (seen[n][1] if n in seen else f"#{n}") for n in nums}
619	    order = [names[n] for n in nums]
620	    bad = {names[n] for n in nums if n not in seen or not seen[n][0]}
621	    return {"passed": sum(1 for n in seen if seen[n][0]), "total": total, "order": order, "bad": bad}

43	def git(repo, *args, binary=False):
44	    cmd = ["git", "-C", repo, "-c", "core.quotepath=off", "-c", "diff.noprefix=false", *args]
45	    p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, env=_git_env())
46	    if p.returncode != 0:
47	        raise RuntimeError(f"git {' '.join(args[:2])} failed: {p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace').strip()}")
48	    return p.stdout if binary else p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")

85	def commits_since(repo, since):
86	    raw = git(repo, "log", f"--since={since}", "--no-merges", "--format=%H%x1f%P%x1f%cs%x1f%s%x1e")
87	    for rec in raw.split("\x1e"):
88	        rec = rec.strip("\n")
89	        if not rec:
90	            continue
91	        sha, parents, date, subject = (rec.split("\x1f") + ["", "", ""])[:4]
92	        yield sha, parents.split(), date, subject

95	def changed_files(repo, parent, sha):
96	    raw = git(repo, "diff", "--no-renames", "--name-status", "-z", parent, sha)
97	    items = raw.split("\0")
98	    files = []
99	    i = 0
100	    while i + 1 < len(items):
101	        status, path = items[i], items[i + 1]
102	        files.append((status[:1], path))
103	        i += 2
104	    return files

107	def numstat(repo, parent, sha, paths=None):
108	    args = ["diff", "--no-renames", "--numstat", parent, sha]
109	    if paths:
110	        args += ["--", *paths]
111	    rows = []
112	    for line in git(repo, *args).splitlines():
113	        a, d, p = line.split("\t", 2)
114	        rows.append((a, d, p))
115	    return rows

118	def blob(repo, commit, path):
119	    """(mode, bytes) of path at commit, or None when absent."""
120	    ls = git(repo, "ls-tree", "-z", commit, "--", path).split("\0")[0]
121	    if not ls:
122	        return None
123	    meta, _ = ls.split("\t", 1)
124	    mode, kind, obj = meta.split()
125	    if kind != "blob":
126	        return None
127	    return mode, git(repo, "cat-file", "blob", obj, binary=True)

131	    args = ["ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "--name-only", commit]
132	    if prefix:
133	        args += ["--", prefix]
134	    return [p for p in git(repo, *args).split("\0") if p]

138	def write_file(root, rel, data):
139	    if not safe_path(rel):
140	        raise ValueError(f"unsafe path: {rel!r}")
141	    dest = os.path.join(root, rel)
142	    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dest), exist_ok=True)
143	    with open(dest, "wb") as fh:

147	def put_from(repo, commit, rel, root, dest_rel=None):
148	    b = blob(repo, commit, rel)
149	    if b is None:
150	        return False
151	    mode, data = b
152	    if mode == "120000":
153	        raise ValueError(f"symlink in history: {rel}")
154	    write_file(root, dest_rel or rel, data)
155	    return True

158	def helper_files(repo, commit, test_paths):
159	    """Test infrastructure the tests rely on: conftest.py up to the root, helpers in each test dir, root runner configs."""
160	    have = set(tree_files(repo, commit))
161	    found = set()
162	    for t in test_paths:
163	        d = os.path.dirname(t)
164	        parts = d.split("/") if d else []
165	        for i in range(len(parts) + 1):
166	            c = "/".join(parts[:i] + ["conftest.py"])
167	            if c in have:
168	                found.add(c)
169	        for f in have:
170	            if os.path.dirname(f) == d and f not in test_paths:
171	                base = os.path.basename(f)
172	                if base in ("conftest.py", "__init__.py") or base.endswith(".bash") or "helper" in base:
173	                    found.add(f)
174	    for f in INFRA_ROOT_FILES:
175	        if f in have:
176	            found.add(f)
177	    return sorted(found)

180	def sibling_files(repo, commit, sources, roots, exclude):
181	    """The other non-test files in each touched source file's directory (the modules it most likely imports)."""
182	    dirs = {os.path.dirname(p) for p in sources}
183	    out = []
184	    for f in tree_files(repo, commit):
185	        if os.path.dirname(f) in dirs and f not in exclude and not is_test(f) and safe_path(f) \
186	                and not mount_owned(f) and under_roots(f, roots):
187	            out.append(f)
188	    return sorted(out)

191	def counts(output, runner):
192	    if runner == "bats":
193	        passed = len(re.findall(r"^ok ", output, re.M))
194	        failed = len(re.findall(r"^not ok ", output, re.M))
195	        return passed, failed
196	    tail = output.strip().splitlines()[-1] if output.strip() else ""
197	    num = lambda w: sum(int(n) for n in re.findall(r"(\d+) " + w, tail))
198	    return num("passed"), num("failed") + num("errors?")

201	def run_tests(tree, cmd, runner):
202	    """Run the task's test command under env -i (plus the host's user base so a user-site pytest is found)."""
203	    home = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="seed-home.")
204	    env = {"PATH": os.environ.get("PATH", "/usr/bin:/bin"), "HOME": home, "LC_ALL": "C",
205	           "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1", "PYTHONUSERBASE": site.getuserbase()}
206	    argv = list(cmd)
207	    if runner == "pytest":
208	        argv = argv[:3] + ["-p", "no:cacheprovider"] + argv[3:]
209	    elif runner == "bats" and os.environ.get("LOA_SEED_BATS"):
210	        argv[0] = os.environ["LOA_SEED_BATS"]
211	    try:
212	        p = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=tree, env=env, capture_output=True, timeout=RUN_TIMEOUT)
213	        text = (p.stdout + p.stderr).decode("utf-8", "replace")
214	        rc = p.returncode
215	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
216	        text, rc = "timeout", 124
217	    except OSError as e:
218	        text, rc = f"cannot run {argv[0]}: {e}", 127
219	    finally:
220	        shutil.rmtree(home, ignore_errors=True)
221	    passed, failed = counts(text, runner)
222	    return rc, passed, failed

251	def sanitise(text, stems):
252	    """Agent-facing text from a commit subject: no control characters, paths, file names, test names, grader words."""
253	    text = "".join(c if c.isprintable() else " " for c in text)
254	    words = []
255	    for w in text.split():
256	        if "/" in w or re.search(r"\.(py|sh|bats|js|ts|mjs|json|ya?ml|md|toml|cfg|ini|txt|patch)\b", w) \
257	                or re.match(r"[\W]*test_\w+", w) or "hidden" in w.lower() \
258	                or any(s and s.lower() in w.lower() for s in stems):
259	            words.append("…")
260	        else:
261	            words.append(w)
262	    return re.sub(r"(… ?)+", "… ", " ".join(words)).strip() or "the change"

282	        "regression_command: null",
283	        f"reference_patch: {ref_patch}",
284	        f"grader_protected: {yq(protected)}",

293	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- selection
294	def classify(mode, repo, sha, parents, roots):
295	    """('candidate', files) | ('refused', path) | ('skipped', reason)."""
296	    if len(parents) != 1:
297	        return "skipped", "not a single-parent commit"
298	    files = changed_files(repo, parents[0], sha)
299	    for _, p in files:
300	        if not safe_path(p):
301	            return "refused", "unsafe path " + json.dumps(p)
302	    for _, p in files:
303	        if mount_owned(p):
304	            return "refused", p
305	    for _, p in files:
306	        if not under_roots(p, roots):
307	            return "skipped", f"outside the allowed roots: {p}"
308	    for a, d, p in numstat(repo, parents[0], sha):
309	        if a == "-" or d == "-":
310	            return "skipped", f"binary change: {p}"
311	    tests = [p for _, p in files if is_test(p)]
312	    sources = [p for _, p in files if not is_test(p)]
313	    if mode == "bugfix":
314	        if not tests:
315	            return "skipped", "no test file touched"
316	        if not sources:
317	            return "skipped", "no source file touched"
318	        added_or_modified = [p for s, p in files if is_test(p) and s in "AM"]
319	        runners = {runner_of(p) for p in added_or_modified} - {None}
320	        if not runners:
321	            return "skipped", "no runnable test file (test_*.py, *_test.py, *.bats) added or changed"
322	        if len(runners) > 1:
323	            return "skipped", "mixed test runners (pytest and bats)"
324	    else:
325	        if tests:
326	            return "skipped", f"touches a test file: {tests[0]}"
327	        if len(sources) < 2:
328	            return "skipped", f"touches {len(sources)} source file(s), want at least 2"
329	    return "candidate", files

342	def covering_tests(repo, parent, sources, roots):
343	    """Test files at parent (under the roots) that name a touched source file."""
344	    names = set()
345	    for s in sources:
346	        base = os.path.basename(s)
347	        names.add(base)
348	        if base.endswith(".py"):
349	            names.add(base[:-3])
350	    pats = [re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])" + re.escape(n) + r"(?![A-Za-z0-9_])") for n in sorted(names)]
351	    hits = []
352	    for r in roots:
353	        for f in tree_files(repo, parent, r):
354	            if not is_test(f) or runner_of(f) is None or not safe_path(f) or mount_owned(f):
355	                continue
356	            b = blob(repo, parent, f)
357	            if b is None or b[0] == "120000":
358	                continue
359	            text = b[1].decode("utf-8", "replace")
360	            if any(p.search(text) for p in pats):
361	                hits.append(f)
362	    return sorted(set(hits))[:MAX_COVERING_TESTS]

370	def build_bugfix(repo, sha, parent, date, subject, files, tid, stage, no_secrets, roots):
371	    tdir = os.path.join(stage, tid)
372	    fx = os.path.join(tdir, "fixture")
373	    os.makedirs(fx)
374	    tests_am = [p for s, p in files if is_test(p) and s in "AM"]
375	    sources = [p for s, p in files if not is_test(p)]
376	    runner = {runner_of(p) for p in tests_am} - {None}
377	    runner = runner.pop()
378	    for p in sources:
379	        put_from(repo, parent, p, fx)
380	    for p in sibling_files(repo, parent, sources, roots, set(sources) | set(tests_am)):
381	        put_from(repo, parent, p, fx)
382	    for p in tests_am:
383	        put_from(repo, parent, p, fx)          # the base version of a changed test (absent when added)
384	    protected = [h for h in helper_files(repo, parent, tests_am) if h not in tests_am and h not in sources]
385	    for h in protected:
386	        put_from(repo, parent, h, fx)
387	    hidden = os.path.join(tdir, "hidden")
388	    manifest = {"files": []}
389	    for p in tests_am:
390	        put_from(repo, sha, p, hidden, "tests/" + p)
391	        manifest["files"].append({"src": "tests/" + p, "dest": p})
392	    write_file(hidden, "manifest.json", (json.dumps(manifest) + "\n").encode())
393	    diff = git(repo, "diff", "--no-color", "--no-ext-diff", "--no-renames", "--src-prefix=a/", "--dst-prefix=b/",
394	               parent, sha, "--", *sources, binary=True)
395	    write_file(hidden, "reference.patch", diff)
396	    runnable = [p for p in tests_am if runner_of(p)]
397	    test_cmd = (["python3", "-m", "pytest", "-q"] if runner == "pytest" else ["bats"]) + test_dirs(runnable)
398	
399	    # proof: red at base, green at reference (hidden tests overlaid on both)
400	    work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="seed-proof.")
401	    try:
402	        base, ref = os.path.join(work, "base"), os.path.join(work, "ref")
403	        copy_tree(fx, base)
404	        overlay(tdir, base, manifest)
405	        rc_b, pass_b, fail_b = run_tests(base, test_cmd, runner)
406	        copy_tree(fx, ref)
407	        if not apply_patch(ref, os.path.join(hidden, "reference.patch")):
408	            return None, "the reference patch does not apply to the fixture"
409	        overlay(tdir, ref, manifest)
410	        rc_r, pass_r, fail_r = run_tests(ref, test_cmd, runner)
411	    finally:
412	        shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
413	    if rc_b == 0 or fail_b < 1:
414	        return None, f"not red at base (exit {rc_b}, {fail_b} failed, {pass_b} passed)"
415	    if rc_r != 0 or fail_r > 0 or pass_r < 1:
416	        return None, f"not green at reference (exit {rc_r}, {fail_r} failed, {pass_r} passed)"
417	    proof = f"red {fail_b} failed / green {pass_r} passed"
418	
419	    stems = [os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(p))[0] for p in tests_am]
420	    rest = sanitise(subject_rest(subject), stems)
421	    criterion = f"the behaviour this change describes holds: {rest}; the checks for it pass and the existing behaviour is unchanged"
422	    hidden_list = ", ".join("hidden/tests/" + p for p in runnable)
423	    success = (f"{hidden_list} (overlaid at {', '.join(runnable)}) passes {pass_r} of {pass_r} under {' '.join(test_cmd)}; "
424	               f"red at base ({fail_b} failed), green with hidden/reference.patch")
425	    source = {"kind": "loa-history", "fix_commit": sha, "base_commit": parent, "date": date}
426	    write_file(tdir, "task.yaml", task_yaml(tid, "bugfix", source, criterion, success, test_cmd,
427	                                           "hidden/reference.patch", protected, SUITE_VERSION).encode())
428	    task_md = (f"# Task: {rest}\n\n"
429	               f"**Bug (observed):** with the code as it is, {fail_b} of {fail_b + pass_b} checks for this behaviour fail "
430	               f"when the test command below runs.\n\n"
431	               f"**Expected:** {rest}. Every check passes and behaviour elsewhere is unchanged.\n\n"
432	               f"Fix the bug in place and add a regression test of your own. Run the tests with `{' '.join(test_cmd)}`.\n")
433	    write_file(tdir, "TASK.md", task_md.encode())
434	    if not secrets_clean(no_secrets, tdir):
435	        return "secret", "a secret pattern in the materialised task"
436	    return tdir, proof

439	def build_refactor(repo, sha, parent, date, subject, files, tid, stage, no_secrets, roots):
440	    sources = [p for s, p in files if not is_test(p)]
441	    tests = covering_tests(repo, parent, sources, roots)
442	    runners = {runner_of(t) for t in tests}
443	    if not tests:
444	        return "skip", "no test at the parent names a touched file"
445	    if len(runners) > 1:
446	        return "skip", "the covering tests mix pytest and bats"
447	    runner = runners.pop()
448	    tdir = os.path.join(stage, tid)
449	    fx = os.path.join(tdir, "fixture")
450	    os.makedirs(fx)
451	    for p in sources:
452	        put_from(repo, parent, p, fx)
453	    for p in sibling_files(repo, parent, sources, roots, set(sources) | set(tests)):
454	        put_from(repo, parent, p, fx)
455	    for t in tests:
456	        put_from(repo, parent, t, fx)
457	    protected = [h for h in helper_files(repo, parent, tests) if h not in tests and h not in sources]
458	    for h in protected:
459	        put_from(repo, parent, h, fx)
460	    hidden = os.path.join(tdir, "hidden")
461	    diff = git(repo, "diff", "--no-color", "--no-ext-diff", "--no-renames", "--src-prefix=a/", "--dst-prefix=b/",
462	               parent, sha, binary=True)
463	    write_file(hidden, "reference.patch", diff)
464	    write_file(hidden, "manifest.json", b'{"files": []}\n')
465	    test_cmd = (["python3", "-m", "pytest", "-q"] if runner == "pytest" else ["bats"]) + test_dirs(tests)
466	
467	    work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="seed-proof.")
468	    try:
469	        base, ref = os.path.join(work, "base"), os.path.join(work, "ref")
470	        copy_tree(fx, base)
471	        rc_b, pass_b, fail_b = run_tests(base, test_cmd, runner)
472	        copy_tree(fx, ref)
473	        if not apply_patch(ref, os.path.join(hidden, "reference.patch")):
474	            return None, "the reference patch does not apply to the fixture"
475	        rc_r, pass_r, fail_r = run_tests(ref, test_cmd, runner)
476	    finally:
477	        shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
478	    if rc_b != 0 or fail_b > 0 or pass_b < 1:
479	        return None, f"suite not green at base (exit {rc_b}, {fail_b} failed, {pass_b} passed)"
480	    if rc_r != 0 or fail_r > 0 or pass_r < 1:
481	        return None, f"suite not green at reference (exit {rc_r}, {fail_r} failed, {pass_r} passed)"
482	    proof = f"green at base ({pass_b} passed) / green at reference ({pass_r} passed)"
483	
484	    rows = numstat(repo, parent, sha)
485	    churn = {"files": len(rows), "insertions": sum(int(a) for a, _, _ in rows), "deletions": sum(int(d) for _, d, _ in rows)}
486	    rest = sanitise(subject_rest(subject), [])
487	    criterion = f"the structure this change describes is in place: {rest}; the existing suite stays green without edits"
488	    success = (f"structural check (to be authored under hidden/structural/) red at base and green with hidden/reference.patch; "
489	               f"{' '.join(test_cmd)} passes {pass_b} of {pass_b} at base and {pass_r} of {pass_r} at reference")
490	    source = {"kind": "loa-history", "fix_commit": sha, "base_commit": parent, "date": date, "churn": churn}
491	    write_file(tdir, "task.yaml", task_yaml(tid, "refactor", source, criterion, success, test_cmd,
492	                                           "hidden/reference.patch", protected, SUITE_VERSION).encode())
493	    task_md = (f"# Task: {rest}\n\n"
494	               f"**Refactor:** {rest}.\n\n"
495	               f"**Unchanged behaviour:** the existing suite must stay green without edits. Run it with `{' '.join(test_cmd)}`.\n")
496	    write_file(tdir, "TASK.md", task_md.encode())
497	    if not secrets_clean(no_secrets, tdir):
498	        return "secret", "a secret pattern in the materialised task"
499	    return tdir, proof + "\t" + json.dumps(churn)

295	    """('candidate', files) | ('refused', path) | ('skipped', reason)."""
296	    if len(parents) != 1:

298	    files = changed_files(repo, parents[0], sha)

302	    for _, p in files:

305	    for _, p in files:
306	        if not under_roots(p, roots):

308	    for a, d, p in numstat(repo, parents[0], sha):
309	        if a == "-" or d == "-":

311	    tests = [p for _, p in files if is_test(p)]
312	    sources = [p for _, p in files if not is_test(p)]
313	    if mode == "bugfix":

316	        if not sources:

318	        added_or_modified = [p for s, p in files if is_test(p) and s in "AM"]

396	    runnable = [p for p in tests_am if runner_of(p)]
397	    test_cmd = (["python3", "-m", "pytest", "-q"] if runner == "pytest" else ["bats"]) + test_dirs(runnable)
398	
399	    # proof: red at base, green at reference (hidden tests overlaid on both)
400	    work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="seed-proof.")
401	    try:
402	        base, ref = os.path.join(work, "base"), os.path.join(work, "ref")
403	        copy_tree(fx, base)
404	        overlay(tdir, base, manifest)
405	        rc_b, pass_b, fail_b = run_tests(base, test_cmd, runner)
406	        copy_tree(fx, ref)
407	        if not apply_patch(ref, os.path.join(hidden, "reference.patch")):
408	            return None, "the reference patch does not apply to the fixture"
409	        overlay(tdir, ref, manifest)
410	        rc_r, pass_r, fail_r = run_tests(ref, test_cmd, runner)
411	    finally:
412	        shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
413	    if rc_b == 0 or fail_b < 1:
414	        return None, f"not red at base (exit {rc_b}, {fail_b} failed, {pass_b} passed)"
415	    if rc_r != 0 or fail_r > 0 or pass_r < 1:
416	        return None, f"not green at reference (exit {rc_r}, {fail_r} failed, {pass_r} passed)"
417	    proof = f"red {fail_b} failed / green {pass_r} passed"
418	
419	    stems = [os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(p))[0] for p in tests_am]
420	    rest = sanitise(subject_rest(subject), stems)
421	    criterion = f"the behaviour this change describes holds: {rest}; the checks for it pass and the existing behaviour is unchanged"
422	    hidden_list = ", ".join("hidden/tests/" + p for p in runnable)
423	    success = (f"{hidden_list} (overlaid at {', '.join(runnable)}) passes {pass_r} of {pass_r} under {' '.join(test_cmd)}; "
424	               f"red at base ({fail_b} failed), green with hidden/reference.patch")
425	    source = {"kind": "loa-history", "fix_commit": sha, "base_commit": parent, "date": date}
426	    write_file(tdir, "task.yaml", task_yaml(tid, "bugfix", source, criterion, success, test_cmd,
427	                                           "hidden/reference.patch", protected, SUITE_VERSION).encode())
428	    task_md = (f"# Task: {rest}\n\n"
429	               f"**Bug (observed):** with the code as it is, {fail_b} of {fail_b + pass_b} checks for this behaviour fail "
430	               f"when the test command below runs.\n\n"
431	               f"**Expected:** {rest}. Every check passes and behaviour elsewhere is unchanged.\n\n"
432	               f"Fix the bug in place and add a regression test of your own. Run the tests with `{' '.join(test_cmd)}`.\n")
433	    write_file(tdir, "TASK.md", task_md.encode())
434	    if not secrets_clean(no_secrets, tdir):
435	        return "secret", "a secret pattern in the materialised task"
436	    return tdir, proof
437	
438	
439	def build_refactor(repo, sha, parent, date, subject, files, tid, stage, no_secrets, roots):
440	    sources = [p for s, p in files if not is_test(p)]
441	    tests = covering_tests(repo, parent, sources, roots)
442	    runners = {runner_of(t) for t in tests}
443	    if not tests:
444	        return "skip", "no test at the parent names a touched file"
445	    if len(runners) > 1:
446	        return "skip", "the covering tests mix pytest and bats"
447	    runner = runners.pop()
448	    tdir = os.path.join(stage, tid)
449	    fx = os.path.join(tdir, "fixture")
450	    os.makedirs(fx)
451	    for p in sources:
452	        put_from(repo, parent, p, fx)
453	    for p in sibling_files(repo, parent, sources, roots, set(sources) | set(tests)):
454	        put_from(repo, parent, p, fx)
455	    for t in tests:
456	        put_from(repo, parent, t, fx)
457	    protected = [h for h in helper_files(repo, parent, tests) if h not in tests and h not in sources]
458	    for h in protected:
459	        put_from(repo, parent, h, fx)
460	    hidden = os.path.join(tdir, "hidden")
461	    diff = git(repo, "diff", "--no-color", "--no-ext-diff", "--no-renames", "--src-prefix=a/", "--dst-prefix=b/",
462	               parent, sha, binary=True)
463	    write_file(hidden, "reference.patch", diff)
464	    write_file(hidden, "manifest.json", b'{"files": []}\n')
465	    test_cmd = (["python3", "-m", "pytest", "-q"] if runner == "pytest" else ["bats"]) + test_dirs(tests)
466	
467	    work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="seed-proof.")
468	    try:
469	        base, ref = os.path.join(work, "base"), os.path.join(work, "ref")
470	        copy_tree(fx, base)
471	        rc_b, pass_b, fail_b = run_tests(base, test_cmd, runner)
472	        copy_tree(fx, ref)
473	        if not apply_patch(ref, os.path.join(hidden, "reference.patch")):
474	            return None, "the reference patch does not apply to the fixture"
475	        rc_r, pass_r, fail_r = run_tests(ref, test_cmd, runner)
476	    finally:
477	        shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
478	    if rc_b != 0 or fail_b > 0 or pass_b < 1:
479	        return None, f"suite not green at base (exit {rc_b}, {fail_b} failed, {pass_b} passed)"
480	    if rc_r != 0 or fail_r > 0 or pass_r < 1:
481	        return None, f"suite not green at reference (exit {rc_r}, {fail_r} failed, {pass_r} passed)"
482	    proof = f"green at base ({pass_b} passed) / green at reference ({pass_r} passed)"
483	
484	    rows = numstat(repo, parent, sha)
485	    churn = {"files": len(rows), "insertions": sum(int(a) for a, _, _ in rows), "deletions": sum(int(d) for _, d, _ in rows)}
486	    rest = sanitise(subject_rest(subject), [])
487	    criterion = f"the structure this change describes is in place: {rest}; the existing suite stays green without edits"
488	    success = (f"structural check (to be authored under hidden/structural/) red at base and green with hidden/reference.patch; "
489	               f"{' '.join(test_cmd)} passes {pass_b} of {pass_b} at base and {pass_r} of {pass_r} at reference")
490	    source = {"kind": "loa-history", "fix_commit": sha, "base_commit": parent, "date": date, "churn": churn}
491	    write_file(tdir, "task.yaml", task_yaml(tid, "refactor", source, criterion, success, test_cmd,
492	                                           "hidden/reference.patch", protected, SUITE_VERSION).encode())
493	    task_md = (f"# Task: {rest}\n\n"
494	               f"**Refactor:** {rest}.\n\n"
495	               f"**Unchanged behaviour:** the existing suite must stay green without edits. Run it with `{' '.join(test_cmd)}`.\n")
496	    write_file(tdir, "TASK.md", task_md.encode())
497	    if not secrets_clean(no_secrets, tdir):
498	        return "secret", "a secret pattern in the materialised task"
499	    return tdir, proof + "\t" + json.dumps(churn)
500	
501	
502	def secrets_clean(no_secrets, tdir):
503	    if not no_secrets:
504	        return True
505	    p = subprocess.run(["bash", no_secrets, tdir], capture_output=True)
506	    return p.returncode == 0
507	
508	
509	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- main
510	SUITE_VERSION = 1
511	
512	
513	def parse(argv):
514	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="seed-tasks", add_help=False)
515	    ap.add_argument("mode", choices=("bugfix", "refactor"))
516	    ap.add_argument("--repo-default", required=True)
517	    ap.add_argument("--no-secrets", default="")
518	    ap.add_argument("--since", required=True)
519	    ap.add_argument("--select", type=int, default=4)
520	    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
521	    ap.add_argument("--repo")
522	    ap.add_argument("--paths", default=DEFAULT_PATHS)
523	    ap.add_argument("--suite-version", type=int, default=1)
524	    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
525	    try:
526	        a = ap.parse_args(argv)
527	    except SystemExit:
528	        raise Usage("bad arguments (see --help)")
529	    try:
530	        datetime.date.fromisoformat(a.since)
531	    except ValueError:
532	        raise Usage(f"--since must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {a.since!r}")
533	    if a.select < 1:
534	        raise Usage("--select must be at least 1")
535	    if a.suite_version < 1:
536	        raise Usage("--suite-version must be at least 1")
537	    a.repo = a.repo or a.repo_default
538	    if subprocess.run(["git", "-C", a.repo, "rev-parse", "--git-dir"], capture_output=True).returncode != 0:
539	        raise Usage(f"not a git repository: {a.repo}")
540	    roots = [r.strip().strip("/") for r in a.paths.split(",") if r.strip().strip("/")]
541	    if not roots or any(not safe_path(r) or mount_owned(r) for r in roots):
542	        raise Usage(f"--paths must be relative roots outside the mount-owned paths: {a.paths!r}")
543	    a.roots = roots
544	    return a
545	
546	
547	def main(argv):
548	    global SUITE_VERSION
549	    try:
550	        a = parse(argv)
551	    except Usage as e:
552	        print(f"seed-{a_mode(argv)}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
553	        return 2
554	    SUITE_VERSION = a.suite_version
555	    name = f"seed-{a.mode}"
556	    cands, refused, skipped = [], 0, 0
557	    for sha, parents, date, subject in commits_since(a.repo, a.since):
558	        if not SUBJECT[a.mode].match(subject):
559	            continue
560	        verdict, detail = classify(a.mode, a.repo, sha, parents, a.roots)
561	        if verdict == "refused":
562	            refused += 1
563	            out(f"refused {sha[:12]}: {detail}")
564	        elif verdict == "skipped":
565	            skipped += 1
566	            out(f"skipped {sha[:12]}: {detail}")
567	        else:
568	            cands.append((sha, parents[0], date, subject, detail))
569	            out(f"candidate {sha[:12]} {date} {''.join(c if c.isprintable() else ' ' for c in subject)}")
570	    selected = cands[: a.select]
571	    if a.dry_run:
572	        out(f"{name}: {len(cands)} candidate(s), {refused} refused, {skipped} skipped; dry run, nothing written")
573	        return 0
574	    tasks_dir = os.path.join(a.out, "tasks")
575	    stage = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="seed-stage.")
576	    written = failed = 0
577	    taken = set()
578	    try:
579	        for sha, parent, date, subject, files in selected:
580	            tid = next_id(tasks_dir, ID_PREFIX[a.mode], taken)
581	            try:
582	                if a.mode == "bugfix":
583	                    tdir, info = build_bugfix(a.repo, sha, parent, date, subject, files, tid, stage, a.no_secrets, a.roots)
584	                else:
585	                    tdir, info = build_refactor(a.repo, sha, parent, date, subject, files, tid, stage, a.no_secrets, a.roots)
586	            except (ValueError, RuntimeError, OSError) as e:
587	                tdir, info = None, str(e)
588	            if tdir == "secret":
589	                refused += 1
590	                out(f"refused {sha[:12]}: {info}")
591	                taken.discard(tid)
592	                continue
593	            if tdir == "skip":
594	                skipped += 1
595	                out(f"skipped {sha[:12]}: {info}")
596	                taken.discard(tid)
597	                continue
598	            if tdir is None:
599	                failed += 1
600	                out(f"proof-failed {sha[:12]}: {info}")
601	                taken.discard(tid)
602	                continue
603	            os.makedirs(tasks_dir, exist_ok=True)
604	            shutil.move(tdir, os.path.join(tasks_dir, tid))
605	            written += 1
606	            if a.mode == "bugfix":
607	                out(f"proof {tid} {sha[:12]}: {info}")
608	            else:
609	                proof, churn = info.split("\t")
610	                c = json.loads(churn)
611	                out(f"proof {tid} {sha[:12]}: {proof}")
612	                out(f"churn {tid}: files {c['files']}, insertions {c['insertions']}, deletions {c['deletions']}")
613	                out(f"todo {tid}: author the structural check under hidden/structural/, list it in hidden/manifest.json "
614	                    f"and set structural_check (validate-suite.sh requires it for refactor)")
615	            out(f"wrote {os.path.join(tasks_dir, tid)}")
616	    finally:
617	        shutil.rmtree(stage, ignore_errors=True)
618	    out(f"{name}: {len(cands)} candidate(s), {refused} refused, {skipped} skipped; "
619	        f"selected {len(selected)}, written {written}, proof failed {failed}")
620	    return 1 if failed else 0
621	
622	
623	def a_mode(argv):
624	    return argv[0] if argv and argv[0] in ("bugfix", "refactor") else "tasks"
625	
626	
627	if __name__ == "__main__":
628	    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

185	  mkdir -p "$rd/sandbox" "$rd/snapshots" "$rd/transcripts" "$rd/eval" "$rd/meta"
186	  echo "$id" > "$rd.task"   # beside the run dir, for apply_ref
187	  if [[ -d "$td/fixture" ]]; then cp -a "$td/fixture/." "$rd/sandbox/"
188	  else mkdir -p "$rd/sandbox/pr"; cp -a "$T/prs/pr-77/." "$rd/sandbox/pr/"; fi
189	  sg "$rd" init -q
190	  printf '%s\n' '/.claude/' '/CLAUDE.md' '/.loa.config.yaml' '/grimoires/' '/.run/' '/.beads/' '/.eval/' >> "$rd/sandbox/.git/info/exclude"
191	  sg "$rd" add -A; sg "$rd" commit -q --allow-empty -m base
192	  jq -n --arg b "$(sg "$rd" rev-parse HEAD)" '{base: $b}' > "$rd/snapshots/index.json"
193	  mkdir -p "$rd/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1" "$rd/sandbox/.claude"
194	  echo "# mount" > "$rd/sandbox/CLAUDE.md"
195	  printf '{"run_id": "r-%s", "status": "completed", "arm": "a1_full"}\n' "$id" > "$rd/meta/pipeline.json"
196	  echo a1_full > "$rd/meta/arm"
197	}
198	# snap <run-dir> <LABEL>: commit and bundle the sandbox as pipeline-run.sh does after IMPLEMENT / FIX
199	snap() {
200	  local rd="$1" L="$2" c k
201	  sg "$rd" add -A; sg "$rd" commit -q --allow-empty -m "snapshot $L"
202	  c="$(sg "$rd" rev-parse HEAD)"; k="$(printf '%s' "$L" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
203	  sg "$rd" bundle create -q "$rd/snapshots/$L.bundle" HEAD
204	  jq --arg k "$k" --arg c "$c" '.[$k] = $c' "$rd/snapshots/index.json" > "$rd/snapshots/i.tmp" && mv "$rd/snapshots/i.tmp" "$rd/snapshots/index.json"
205	}
206	# verdict <run-dir> review|audit <VERDICT> [body]
207	verdict() {
208	  local f=engineer-feedback.md; [[ "$2" == audit ]] && f=auditor-sprint-feedback.md
209	  printf '# Feedback\n\n%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":1}} -->\n' "${4:-}" "$2" "$3" \
210	    > "$1/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/$f"
211	}
212	apply_ref() { patch -s -p1 -d "$1/sandbox" < "$S/tasks/$(cat "$1.task")/hidden/reference.patch"; }
213	# tool_use <run-dir> <LABEL> <tool> <input-json>: one assistant tool_use event line
214	tool_use() {
215	  jq -cn --arg t "$3" --argjson i "$4" '{type: "assistant", message: {content: [{type: "tool_use", name: $t, input: $i}]}}' \
216	    >> "$1/transcripts/events-$2.jsonl"
217	}
218	grade() { run "$GRADER" "$@" --suite-root "$S" --allow-unfrozen --docker-bin "$T/docker"; }
219	tree_digest() {
220	  python3 -I -c '
221	import hashlib, os, sys
222	h = hashlib.sha256(); root = sys.argv[1]
223	for r, ds, fs in os.walk(root):
224	    ds.sort()
225	    for n in sorted(ds + fs):
226	        p = os.path.join(r, n); h.update(os.path.relpath(p, root).encode() + b"\0")
227	        if os.path.islink(p): h.update(b"L" + os.readlink(p).encode())
228	        elif os.path.isfile(p): h.update(open(p, "rb").read())
229	print(h.hexdigest())' "$1"
230	}
231	G() { jq -r "$1" "$RD/grade.json"; }

221	import hashlib, os, sys
222	h = hashlib.sha256(); root = sys.argv[1]
223	for r, ds, fs in os.walk(root):
224	    ds.sort()
225	    for n in sorted(ds + fs):
226	        p = os.path.join(r, n); h.update(os.path.relpath(p, root).encode() + b"\0")
227	        if os.path.islink(p): h.update(b"L" + os.readlink(p).encode())
228	        elif os.path.isfile(p): h.update(open(p, "rb").read())
229	print(h.hexdigest())' "$1"

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# evals/tests/seed-bugfix.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 259 Task 2.2 (SDD §5.14,
+# sprint AC-2.9)
+#
+# seed-bugfix-tasks.sh over a throwaway git repo: a clean fix commit (a Python
+# module + its test, red at the parent, green at the commit) becomes a task
+# whose every field validates; a fix touching .claude/ is refused by name and
+# writes nothing; --dry-run writes nothing; a fix whose test is already green
+# at the parent fails its proof (exit 1, nothing written); a fix outside the
+# allowed roots is skipped; usage errors are exit 2.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+  SEED="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/seed-bugfix-tasks.sh"
+  VS="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sb.XXXXXX")"
+  G="$T/repo"; S="$T/suite"
+  export LOA_EVAL_PHASE_PROMPTS_DIR="$T/no-prompts"
+  python3 -m pytest --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "pytest not importable by python3"
+  git init -q -b main "$G"
+  mkdir -p "$G/tools/mathx/tests" "$G/docs"
+  cat > "$G/tools/mathx/rounding.py" <<'PY'
+def round_half(x):
+    """Round to the nearest integer, halves away from zero."""
+    return int(x + 0.5)
+PY
+  cat > "$G/tools/mathx/tests/conftest.py" <<'PY'
+import os, sys
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))
+PY
+  cat > "$G/tools/mathx/tests/test_rounding.py" <<'PY'
+from rounding import round_half
+
+def test_positive():
+    assert round_half(2.5) == 3
+PY
+  echo "notes" > "$G/docs/README"
+  gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "chore: initial"
+}
+
+teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
+
+gc() { git -C "$G" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t -c commit.gpgsign=false "$@"; }
+
+# the clean fix: negative halves round away from zero; two new test cases
+commit_clean_fix() {
+  cat > "$G/tools/mathx/rounding.py" <<'PY'
+import math
+
+
+def round_half(x):
+    """Round to the nearest integer, halves away from zero."""
+    return int(math.copysign(math.floor(abs(x) + 0.5), x))
+PY
+  cat >> "$G/tools/mathx/tests/test_rounding.py" <<'PY'
+
+def test_negative_half():
+    assert round_half(-2.5) == -3
+
+def test_negative():
+    assert round_half(-1.6) == -2
+PY
+  gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "fix(mathx): negative halves round away from zero"

+commit_claude_fix() {

+  grep -q '2 of 3 checks' "$D/TASK.md"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Security Audit Scope Analysis
# Two-Pass Methodology v1.0
#
# Shows file counts by security-relevant category to understand audit surface.
# Part of Loa's /audit skill enhancement.
#
# Usage: .claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh [OPTIONS]
#   --no-symlinks    Skip symlinks (default: follow)
#   --max-depth N    Limit search depth (default: unlimited)
#   --json           Output as JSON

set -euo pipefail

# Parse arguments
FOLLOW_SYMLINKS=true
MAX_DEPTH=""
OUTPUT_JSON=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case $1 in
    --no-symlinks) FOLLOW_SYMLINKS=false; shift ;;
    --max-depth) MAX_DEPTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json) OUTPUT_JSON=true; shift ;;
    *) echo "Unknown option: $1"; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

# Build find options as array (HIGH-002 remediation - prevents word splitting)
declare -a FIND_OPTS=(-type f)
if [[ "$FOLLOW_SYMLINKS" == "false" ]]; then
  FIND_OPTS=(-type f -not -type l)
fi
if [[ -n "$MAX_DEPTH" ]]; then
  FIND_OPTS=(-maxdepth "$MAX_DEPTH" "${FIND_OPTS[@]}")
fi

# Exclude patterns (POSIX compatible)
EXCLUDE_DIRS="node_modules|\.git|dist|build|\.next|vendor|__pycache__|\.venv"

# Count function with error suppression
# Uses array expansion for safe variable handling
count_files() {
  local pattern="$1"
  local result
  result=$(find . "${FIND_OPTS[@]}" \( -name "*.ts" -o -name "*.js" -o -name "*.py" -o -name "*.go" -o -name "*.java" \) 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -v -E "$EXCLUDE_DIRS" | \
    xargs grep -l "$pattern" 2>/dev/null | wc -l || echo "0")
  echo "$result" | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

count_by_name() {
  local pattern="$1"
  local result
  result=$(find . "${FIND_OPTS[@]}" \( -name "*$pattern*" \) 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -v -E "$EXCLUDE_DIRS" | wc -l || echo "0")
  echo "$result" | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

# Collect metrics

DISS-001 [HIGH] input-validation voice=gpt-5.5-pro anchor=evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:parse_pytest line=576--
  title: [P1] Validate output-derived paths before opening them on the host
  desc: Container output controls `f` without path validation. A malicious submission can emit `ERROR /dev/zero` followed by `1 error in 0.01s`; the host then executes `open('/dev/zero').read()`, consuming memory indefinitely outside the container timeout. Absolute paths, traversal paths and escaping symlinks also permit reads outside the grading tree. Apply containment checks to both this read and `def_line`, require regular files, and bound reads.
  fix: 

DISS-002 [HIGH] input-validation voice=gpt-5.5-pro anchor=evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:run_suite line=638-640
  title: [P1] Reject failed executions before accepting claimed test results
  desc: When output parses, `run_suite` preserves claimed passes regardless of the exit status, and `all_pass` ignores both `rc` and `timed_out`. Submission-controlled code can emit a fabricated summary such as `1000000 passed in 0.01s` and terminate before running hidden tests. The parser requires no corresponding outcome records, so this produces full credit and can mark an APPROVED verdict accurate. Require successful execution and validate claimed results against expected test cases before accepting a pass.
  fix: 

DISS-C-001 [HIGH] input-validation voice=claude-headless anchor=evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:parse_pytest line=546-594
  title: The graded agent (or any code it leaves in sandbox/) fabricates a perfect hidden-test, regression and structural grade; the ablation results are untrustworthy.
  desc: Hidden-test results are derived solely from parsing the stdout of a process that executes agent-controlled code. The hidden tests are overlaid onto the agent's tree and import the agent's modules; the agent's conftest.py / pytest.ini (addopts) / any imported module runs in the same pytest process (container mode even passes -s, so prints go straight to the captured stream). A module can print `PASSED tests/test_x.py::t` lines plus a fake `===== 12 passed in 0.1s =====` summary and call os._exit(0); parse_pytest takes the last matching summary, all_pass() is true and hidden_tests/snapshot_tests/verdict_accuracy are forged. Separately, run_suite (line 631-633) sets passed=total whenever no summary parses and rc==0, so a conftest that os._exit(0)s at import yields a full-score passed/total (only parse_error distinguishes it, and downstream consumers may not check it).
  fix: Do not trust the terminal output. Load a grader-owned pytest plugin via `-p` (mounted read-only from a path outside /workspace) that writes machine-readable results to a second mount (`-v <scratch>:/results`) and cross-check: number of collected hidden node ids must equal the ids statically enumerated from the overlaid files, every id must appear exactly once, and the pytest exit code must be consistent with the counts. Treat a run without a genuine session end (no `short test summary info` block / rc inconsistent with counts) as failed, not parse_error. In run_suite, when no summary parses never set passed=total; set passed=0 regardless of rc.

DISS-C-002 [MEDIUM] authz voice=claude-headless anchor=evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:grade line=1080-1102
  title: Agent-written code turns a red structural check or regression suite green by overwriting the grader's overlaid files between runs on the same tree.
  desc: The same `final` tree is bind-mounted :rw and reused across sequential suite runs: hidden tests (line 1080), then the regression command (1090), then for refactor tasks the structural check (1101). prepare() restores grader_protected paths and overlays hidden files only once, before the first run. Agent code executed during the first run (test import side effects) can rewrite the overlaid structural check, the regression tests, or the protected fixture files at their dest paths in /workspace so that the later runs grade a tampered tree.
  fix: Re-run prepare() (or use a fresh copy of the tree) immediately before every run_suite call, or mount the tree read-only and give pytest a writable tmpfs for caches. Optionally hash the overlaid files after each run and flag any change as tampering in grade.json.

DISS-C-003 [MEDIUM] input-validation voice=claude-headless anchor=evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:def_line line=536-576
  title: The graded agent hangs or crashes the grader process (and the batch) by emitting a crafted node id; limited read oracle on host files.
  desc: Node ids and collection-error paths parsed from the agent-influenced pytest output are joined with os.path.join(tree, path) and opened with .read(). An absolute or `..` path discards the tree prefix, so an `ERROR /dev/zero` or `FAILED /dev/urandom::t` line makes the grader read an infinite device into memory (OOM), an `ERROR tests/fifo` naming a FIFO the agent created inside /workspace during the run blocks the grader forever, and any host file can be opened (a weak oracle: count of `def test` lines). The churn() reader (line 732) likewise reads every sandbox file fully with no size cap.
  fix: Validate every output-derived path with safe_rel(), require it to resolve inside the tree, os.lstat() it and only open S_ISREG files below a size cap (e.g. 2 MiB); never open device nodes, FIFOs or symlinks. Apply the same cap to churn() and to the review/feedback markdown reads.

DISS-C-004 [MEDIUM] other voice=claude-headless anchor=evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:remove_path line=242-242
  title: The graded agent changes the mode of arbitrary directories owned by the grading user (home, ~/.ssh, shared data dirs) to 0700, breaking other processes or users.
  desc: remove_path walks a directory and calls os.chmod(os.path.join(r, d), 0o700) for every entry in `dirs`. os.walk lists symlinks-to-directories in `dirs`, and os.chmod follows symlinks on Linux, so a symlink planted by the agent (copy_tree faithfully recreates sandbox symlinks into grading/final; extract_snapshot keeps in-tree symlinks) is dereferenced and its target is chmod'ed. This is reachable via put_file() → remove_path(dst) when a grader_protected directory collides with an agent directory containing `x -> /home/<grader>`, via fresh_dir(grading) on a re-grade of a run whose previous grading tree has such links, and via the finally-block remove_path(SCRATCH).
  fix: Skip entries where os.path.islink(path) is true before chmod (or use os.chmod(..., follow_symlinks=False) where supported and fall back to skipping), and drop the chmod pass entirely in favour of shutil.rmtree(onerror=...) that chmods only after a failed unlink of a real directory.

DISS-C-005 [MEDIUM] config voice=claude-headless anchor=evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:exec_in_tree line=506-518
  title: Agent code fork-bombs or allocates memory until the grading host is unusable, or leaves immortal containers behind after every grade; a single malicious run stalls the whole batch.
  desc: The docker run has --network none and --read-only but no --memory, --pids-limit, --cpus, --cap-drop or no-new-privileges. The inner `timeout 120` sends only SIGTERM (no -k), which a test process can ignore. When the outer subprocess timeout (180 s) fires, Python kills only the docker CLI client; the container is not named and is never killed, so with --rm it keeps running untouched.
  fix: Add `--memory 1g --memory-swap 1g --pids-limit 256 --cpus 2 --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --name <uuid>`; use `timeout -k 10 120`; on TimeoutExpired run `docker kill <name>`. In host mode apply ulimit -u/-v via a wrapper or refuse (see AG-06).

DISS-C-006 [MEDIUM] authz voice=claude-headless anchor=evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:exec_in_tree line=510-515
  title: A single graded agent exfiltrates grader credentials and the full hidden test suite, or persists on the host, defeating the DEC-0491 isolation goal.

## Executive Summary

The change adds the cycle-130 ablation grader, two task seeders with a shared Python library, the bd-8o5rx generated-path exclusion, the \`source.churn\` schema, regenerated pr-14/pr-15 key manifests (SHA256SUMS verified with \`sha256sum -c\`; only generated-path \`fix_regions\` were removed, defects untouched) and six bats suites. The parts that read history and task metadata are careful: every path is checked with \`safe_rel\`/\`safe_path\` before it touches disk, symlinks in history are refused, mount-owned paths are refused by name, subprocesses are argument vectors, nothing is sourced or eval'd, \`grade.json\` is written atomically and carries ids only.

The weak side is the boundary the grader exists to police: the agent's tree. The grader opens paths it parses out of the *agent-controlled* test process's stdout on the host (\`/dev/zero\`, a FIFO, any host file), accepts a forged summary line or an \`os._exit(0)\` as a full score, reuses one read-write tree across the hidden, regression and structural runs with a single restore, follows planted symlinks when it chmods, runs the grading container with no pids/memory/cpu caps and a SIGTERM-only timeout that leaves an unnamed container alive, and feeds unbounded agent text to a quadratic regex. On the test side, the one assertion that no hidden byte reached the sandbox is a bare \`!\` that bats never evaluates (reproduced), and the dissent-envelope parser never reads \`anchor_line\`, so every defect caught only by the review or audit dissent is graded as missed (verified against this sprint's own envelopes). The measurement this grader produces is the asset; today a single uncooperative sandbox can forge it, stall it, or crash the host running it.

## High Priority Security Issues (Fix Before Deployment)

### [HIGH-001] The hidden-test leak guard cannot fail

**Severity:** HIGH — **Confidence:** high
**File:** \`head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:498\` (also \`:503\`)
**Issue:** The new "frozen-suite layout" test is the only check of AC-2.6 / AC-5.5 ("no byte of any hidden/ file reached the sandbox, its git history or the snapshots"). Two of its three assertions are bare negations inside the test body:
\`\`\`bash
  for f in sealed-case-7f3a sealed-shape-91c2 sealed-patch-c0de; do
    ! grep -rqF "\$f" "\$T/run/sandbox" "\$T/run/snapshots" "\$T/run/transcripts"
  done
  …
  ! git -C "\$T/run/sandbox" grep -q -e 'sealed-' \$revs --
\`\`\`
bash skips both \`set -e\` and the ERR trap for a \`!\`-inverted command, so a sealed marker present in the sandbox, a snapshot or a transcript passes silently. Only line 504 is effective, and only because it is the test's last command. Reproduced on this host's bats 1.13.0: a mid-test \`! grep -q x <<<"x"\` is \`ok\`; the same line last, as \`run !\`, or with \`|| false\` is \`not ok\`.
**Impact:** A guard that cannot fire reports the suite's core confidentiality property as verified while a leak of the hidden tests into the agent's view invalidates the whole ablation.
**Fix:** \`run ! grep -rqF "\$f" …\` (after \`bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0\`) or \`… || false\`, as \`head/evals/tests/seed-bugfix.bats:93\`, \`:109\`, \`:123\` already do. Apply to MED-013 in the same pass.
**Reference:** CWE-754 Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html ; bats-core "run ! command" — https://bats-core.readthedocs.io/en/stable/writing-tests.html#run-test-other-commands

### [HIGH-002] Paths parsed from the agent's test output are opened on the host without containment

**Severity:** HIGH — **Confidence:** high
**File:** \`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:574-576\` (also \`:536\`, \`:566-567\`)
**Issue:** \`parse_pytest\` collects every \`ERROR <node>\` line without \`::\` as a collection-error path and reads it on the host:
\`\`\`python
    for f in coll_err:
        try:
            text = open(os.path.join(tree, f), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
\`\`\`
and \`def_line\` (\`:536\`) does the same with the path half of every \`PASSED|FAILED|… <node>\` id. The stdout comes from a process running the agent's modules (container mode even passes \`-s\`), so one \`print("ERROR /dev/zero")\` before the real summary makes the grader \`open("/dev/zero").read()\` outside the container and its timeout (\`os.path.join("/tree", "/dev/zero") == "/dev/zero"\`, verified); \`ERROR tests/fifo\` naming a FIFO the test run created in the rw \`/workspace\` blocks \`open()\` forever; \`ERROR ../../../etc/passwd\` (\`..\` is not rejected) or an absolute path reads any host file the grading user can, with the count of \`def test\` matches as a weak oracle.
**Impact:** Host memory exhaustion or a hung grader (the batch stalls on one run) and an out-of-tree read primitive, triggered by content the thing under evaluation controls.
**Fix:** Pass every output-derived path through \`safe_rel\`, require \`is_within(tree, …)\`, \`os.lstat\` it and open only \`S_ISREG\` files under a size cap (a few MiB); never follow symlinks; treat anything else as "unknown node" with no read.
**Reference:** CWE-22 Path Traversal — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html ; CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html

### [HIGH-003] Agent-controlled code can forge a full hidden-test score

**Severity:** HIGH — **Confidence:** high (mechanism); the exploit needs a gaming or careless agent
**File:** \`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:631-633\` (also \`:652-653\`, \`:593\`)
**Issue:** Results are derived only from the stdout of a process that imports the agent's modules and runs any non-protected \`conftest.py\`/\`pytest.ini\`. Two independent routes to a perfect score:
\`\`\`python
    if parsed is None:
        total = max(static, 1)
        passed = total if rc == 0 else 0
\`\`\`
a \`conftest.py\` that calls \`os._exit(0)\` at import prints no summary and exits 0 → \`passed == total\` with only \`parse_error: true\` to tell (the row consumer in AG-18 reads \`hidden_test_pass_rate\` from passed/total, \`head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:391\`). Or the module prints \`PASSED tests/test_x.py::t\` lines plus \`===== 7 passed in 0.1s =====\` and exits 0: \`parse_pytest\` takes the last matching summary, \`all_pass\` (\`:652\`) checks neither \`rc\` nor \`timed_out\` nor that the parsed ids match the static case list, so \`hidden_tests\`, \`snapshot_tests\` and \`verdict_accuracy\` are all forged. Review Observations §2 rated this MEDIUM; both dissent voices rate it HIGH/BLOCKING and I agree: the grade is the asset.
**Impact:** The arm comparison DEC-0420 exists for can be gamed to 100% by one line in the sandbox.
**Fix:** Never set \`passed = total\` on a parse failure (passed = 0, \`parse_error\` true); require \`rc == 0\` for \`all_pass\` and \`rc != 0\` ⇔ failures present (a mismatch is \`parse_error\`); cross-check parsed node ids against the statically enumerated hidden cases (each exactly once); load a grader-owned pytest plugin via \`-p\` from a read-only mount that writes results to a second mount, and prefer that over stdout.
**Reference:** CWE-345 Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/345.html ; CWE-807 Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/807.html

### [HIGH-004] Dissent findings never count toward recall

**Severity:** HIGH — **Confidence:** high
**File:** \`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:864-867\`
**Issue:**
\`\`\`python
        fp = f.get("file") or f.get("path")
        ln = f.get("line") or f.get("line_start") or f.get("start_line")
\`\`\`
The real envelopes carry neither: every finding in this sprint's \`adversarial-review.json\` and \`adversarial-audit.json\` is \`{"anchor": "evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:envelope_texts", "anchor_line": 864, "anchor_line_end": 867}\` with no \`file\`/\`path\`/\`line\` (verified with jq; FR-4 contract at \`.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:28\`, \`:608-618\`). ## Medium/Low Priority Issues

### [MED-001] The grading container has no resource caps
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — **Confidence:** high (absence), medium (impact)
- **File:** \`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:506-508\`
- **Issue:** \`docker run --rm --network none --read-only --tmpfs /tmp:rw,size=256m --user …\` — no \`--pids-limit\`, \`--memory\`, \`--cpus\`, \`--cap-drop ALL\` or \`--security-opt no-new-privileges\`. The agent container in pipeline-run uses 512 / 4g / 2 (\`head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:753-755\`), so the grader is the laxer of the two sandboxes for the same code. A fork bomb or allocation loop in agent-authored test code takes the grading host down within the 120 s window. The rw \`/workspace\` mount is also unbounded disk. Confirmed by cross-model review (DISS-C-005).
- **Fix:** Mirror pipeline-run's caps and add \`--cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges\`.
- **Reference:** CWE-400 — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html ; CWE-770 — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html

### [MED-002] SIGTERM-only timeout; a timed-out container is never killed
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — **Confidence:** high
- **File:** \`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:508\`, \`:517-521\`
- **Issue:** The in-container \`timeout 120 …\` has no \`-k\`, so a test process that ignores SIGTERM runs on (\`timeout 1 bash -c 'trap "" TERM; sleep 3'\` runs 3 s, rc 124 — reproduced). At 180 s Python's \`TimeoutExpired\` kills only the \`docker run\` client; the container is unnamed, never \`docker kill\`ed, and keeps its rw mount into \`grading/<label>\`, which the next \`fresh_dir(grading)\` (\`:1053\`) removes under it. Confirmed by cross-model review (DISS-C-005; the review's DISS-C-004).
- **Fix:** \`timeout -k 10 120\`; \`--name <uuid>\` and \`docker kill <name>\` in the \`except\`.
- **Reference:** CWE-404 Improper Resource Shutdown — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/404.html

### [MED-003] Unbounded copy and read of agent files; sparse files balloon
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — **Confidence:** medium
- **File:** \`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:296\` (also \`:732\`, \`:878\`)
- **Issue:** \`copy_tree\` copies every regular sandbox file with \`shutil.copyfile\` and \`churn\` reads each one whole. A sparse file is free to create in the sandbox (\`truncate -s 1T\`) and is materialised in full on copy (300 MB sparse → 300 MB on disk, reproduced), then read into memory. No size cap anywhere on agent-controlled content.
- **Fix:** \`os.lstat\` first; skip or record files above a cap (and \`st_blocks*512 << st_size\` sparse files); stream the churn diff or cap it.

### [MED-005] One restore, three runs on the same read-write tree
- **Severity:** MEDIUM — **Confidence:** high
- **File:** \`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1078-1101\`
- **Issue:** \`prepare(t, final)\` runs once (\`:1078\`); the hidden tests (\`:1080\`), the regression command (\`:1090\`) and the structural check (\`:1101\`) then run sequentially on the same \`final\` tree mounted \`:rw\`.
